items.title: Nvidia 洽谈为 Nscale 西弗吉尼亚 Anthropic 数据中心提供债务担保
items.description: 据 The Information 报道、Bloomberg 佐证，Nvidia 正洽谈为 Nscale 在西弗吉尼亚为 Anthropic 建设的数据中心担保数十亿美元债务融资，Anthropic 已就首栋建筑签署 446 亿美元合同。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/hx5dsruslfiiqhbsro2tvg1n8
items.excerpt:
Nvidia weighs playing the cosigner for Nscale’s AI data center in West Virginia
据 The Information 报道、Bloomberg 佐证，Nvidia 正洽谈为 Nscale 在西弗吉尼亚为 Anthropic 建设的数据中心担保数十亿美元债务融资，Anthropic 已就首栋建筑签署 446 亿美元合同。
报道梳理了 Nvidia 或将为 Nscale 数据中心债务担保的结构与风险背景，读者可借此理解 AI 基建融资链条中的连带风险。
据 The Information 周四报道 ，英伟达正在洽谈为 AI 云服务商 Nscale 在弗吉尼亚州规划的 Anthropic 数据中心提供数十亿美元的债务融资担保。彭博社随后 证实了这一报道 。根据 Nscale 的 IPO 文件 ，仅该项目的第一栋建筑，Anthropic 就签下了 446 亿美元的合同。本质上，这家芯片厂商是在为客户的贷款共同签字，这折射出在投资者对涉及的资金规模 日益不安 之际，AI 行业为维持其建设计划有多拼。
这一拟议安排将帮助 Nscale 为其弗吉尼亚州园区的电力和建设成本获得融资。据 The Information 报道 ，在所谓的剩余价值担保机制下，如果 Nscale 拖欠建设款项，英伟达将介入，暂时接管该设施，并协助寻找买家和新的租户。
对 Nscale 来说，赌注很高。该公司 正寻求上市 ，估值最高达 350 亿美元，尽管外界对其能否兑现雄心勃勃的数据中心项目日益担忧。
Anthropic 与 Nscale 的合同覆盖 Nscale 弗吉尼亚州园区第一栋 460 兆瓦的建筑，该建筑预计将采用英伟达下一代 Vera Rubin 芯片。双方还在讨论 第二笔交易 ，价值约 450 亿美元，涉及另一栋建筑。
Nscale 的项目推进一直不顺。截至 8 月，该公司仅有约 2.5 万块先进 AI 芯片在运行 ，与其计划部署的近 50 万块相比只是零头。其弗吉尼亚州园区本身也麻烦不断。施工现场的径流 不止一次 淹了附近的住宅 。今年 9 月， 经过数月谈判 ，该项目终于获得州政府认证。
本月，微软 退出了 计划在英格兰建设的一处 Nscale 站点，原因是该站点的电网供电被推迟到了 2030 年代。
据 The Information 报道，英伟达一直是该领域的主要资金支持者，向新型云服务商和大客户 提供了约 1700 亿美元 的投资和信贷支持，其中包括 9 月承诺向 Nscale 提供的 10 亿美元可转换融资。
新型云服务商靠出租 AI 算力为生，背后没有现金充裕的核心业务支撑，如今正承受投资者的压力。据 CNBC 报道 ，截至上周，CoreWeave、Nebius 和 IREN 的股价在 10 月均已下跌超过 30%。
这一拟议中的担保将加深英伟达与 Nscale 的财务绑定，同时为其芯片锁定一个大客户。Anthropic 是 AI 算力的最大买家之一，其基础设施支出分散在多家芯片厂商身上。一位投资者对 The Information 表示，Anthropic 的参与很可能正是英伟达有意让 Nscale 项目继续推进的原因。
这些讨论出现之际，Anthropic 正面临 外界质疑 ：它将如何为自己的快速扩张提供资金。该公司本周提交了上市申请，但 Blackstone 已提醒投资者，Anthropic 在 IPO 后可能获得 低于投资级 的信用评级。垃圾级评级会推高 Anthropic 的借贷成本，并可能迫使它继续依赖实力更强的合作伙伴为其债务提供支持。

items.title: OpenRouter 教程：用 Agent SDK 搭建常驻 AI Agent 监控 Hacker News
items.description: OpenRouter 发布教程，演示用 @openrouter/agent 0.11.0 在 TypeScript 中搭建定时运行的常驻 AI Agent，监控 Hacker News 并生成摘要。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/upl3hjjdokqe13w3ieo9opr0v
items.excerpt:
OpenRouter 发布教程，演示用 @openrouter/agent 0.11.0 在 TypeScript 中搭建定时运行的常驻 AI Agent，监控 Hacker News 并生成摘要。
教程给出可直接复用的 TypeScript 代码和真实成本数据，读者可以照着搭一个带限额和人工审批的定时 Agent。
常驻式 AI 智能体是一种按计划自动唤醒的程序：它调用工具查看某些信息，判断哪些内容重要，然后自行采取行动或汇报结果，无需你每次手动触发。在 DevDay 2026 上，OpenAI 发布了 Dots ，这是他们对常驻式智能体的实现。你也可以自己搭建一个，自行选择模型、工具，以及每次运行的花费上限。
本教程中，我们用 TypeScript 和 OpenRouter Agent SDK 搭建一个这样的智能体：它监控 Hacker News 上你选定的主题，把值得一读的内容整理成摘要，在重启后仍记得已经看过哪些内容，并且一旦某次运行的花费达到五美分就立即停止。每次检查的花费在 $0.0003 到 $0.0012 之间。同样的结构适用于任何需要持续运行的智能体，比如监控某个代码仓库或状态页面、然后采取行动的智能体。
一次计划检查。有审批待处理时，本次运行会被跳过；否则它会开启全新对话，并受各项限制约束。
我们的 Agent SDK 负责运行模型和工具调用、施加限制并保存对话，以便暂停的运行能够恢复；而你的代码负责调度，以及维护记录智能体已见故事的文件。如果你想了解 SDK 为你做了什么，我们关于 构建工具调用智能体循环 的教程手写了同样的循环。
你需要 Node.js（我们用的是 22 版）和一个 OpenRouter API 密钥。如果还没有密钥， 快速入门 会带你创建一个。
创建一个项目，安装 SDK、Zod（SDK 用它定义工具输入 schema）和 tsx（用于直接运行 TypeScript），然后让脚本能读取你的密钥：
把 type 设为 module 可以让脚本使用顶层 await。SDK 仍处于 0.x 版本，因此命令中固定使用 0.11.0 。
如果你用 Bun， bun add @openrouter/agent@0.11.0 zod 会安装脚本所需的全部依赖；本教程中运行 npx tsx agent.ts 的地方，你都可以改用 bun agent.ts 。
check_hacker_news 通过 Hacker News 搜索 API 搜索近期故事，只返回智能体尚未看过的内容。
每个工具都有名称、描述、用于输入的 Zod schema，以及一个 execute 函数。如果你来自其他框架，我们关于 各智能体框架如何处理工具调用 schema 的对比展示了六种框架如何定义相同的组成部分。创建 agent.ts ，从导入、设置、记忆和工具开始：
该工具会在把结果交给模型之前，先过滤掉智能体已经看过的报道，这样模型就不必自己记录之前报道过的内容，也不会冒重复报道同一条的风险。
只有在一次运行结束时，新 ID 才会写入 seen.json ，因此中途失败的运行不会丢失它的报道。在此之前，它们保存在 fetched.json 中，重启后依然存在。测试时，我们在一次返回 20 条新报道的搜索之后立刻杀掉了进程。下一次运行继续了未完成的对话（第 2 步），根据保存的搜索结果写出了摘要，并把全部 20 个 ID 加进了 seen.json ，之后的检查发现 0 条新报道。代价是，如果一次运行在写完摘要之后失败，可能会把同一条报道列两次。重复比丢失更容易补救。
工具就位后，下一部分是一次检查， callModel 以智能体循环的方式执行这次检查。它调用模型，执行模型要求的任何工具，把结果送回，并重复这一过程，直到模型完成或触发停止条件。把 runOnce 加到 agent.ts 中；如果你想更深入地了解 callModel ，可以看看我们的 Agent SDK 教程 ：
stopWhen 会在运行达到六步或花费五美分时结束，以先到者为准。在 0.11.0 版本中，SDK 会在各轮工具调用之间检查 停止条件 ，然后关闭工具做一次收尾调用，让智能体写出答案。因此一次运行可能超出限制一到两次模型调用，按每次调用约 $0.0004 计算，也就是不到一美分。
团队频道工具上的 requireApproval: true 会让运行在该工具执行前暂停。SDK 用 status: "awaiting_approval" 和待处理的调用保存对话， result.requiresApproval() 返回 true，函数把请求写入 pending.log ，因此在有人做出决定之前，什么都不会发到你的团队。
state 会在运行过程中保存对话，这让暂停的运行之后能在另一个进程中恢复。任何保存的对话只要不是 complete ，就属于一次未完成的运行，因此 runOnce 会在开始新的检查之前，用相同的指令和工具继续它。这覆盖了已批准工具刚运行完就失败的情况：SDK 已经保存了工具的结果并把对话标记为 in_progress ，所以继续它会把这个结果发给模型，而不是再次运行该工具。只有在恢复的运行返回之后， decisions.json 才会被删除。恢复的运行也可能再次暂停，例如模型在第一条帖子获批后又要求发第二条，因此新运行和恢复的运行共用 finish() ，它会记录任何仍在等待批准的调用。
rmSync(STATE, { force: true }) 让每次新检查都从空对话开始。我们加上这一行，是因为注意到复用对话会把之前每次检查都重新发给模型，导致每次运行都比上一次略贵一些。已见 ID 列表已经携带了智能体从一次检查到下一次所需的一切。

items.title: Why Automated Cells Are Pulling Inspection Onto the Shop Floor
items.description: Key Points Factories installed 542,000 industrial robots in 2024, more than double the number a decade earlier, according to the International Federation of Robotics. As cells run longer and with fewer people, many manufacturers are moving coordinate measuring machines closer to production so parts are checked within minutes of machining. Temperature is the main challenge […]
items.excerpt:
For decades, the coordinate measuring machine lived in a quiet, climate-controlled room down the hall from production. Parts were carried in on a cart, measured in a queue and sent back with a report, sometimes hours later.
As automated cells take on more of the machining work, that walk to the lab is starting to look like the slowest step in the process.
Bringing inspection to the cell does not always require a brand-new machine. Many shops start with refurbished used CMM equipment , and CMMXYZ, an independent measurement solutions provider based in Mississauga, Ontario, restores each unit through a 31-point inspection and completes final calibration on the customer’s own floor.
Automation on the factory floor keeps growing. The International Federation of Robotics reported 542,000 industrial robot installations in 2024, more than double the number recorded ten years earlier, with the global operational stock reaching about 4.66 million units.
In the Americas, installations reached 50,100 units, including 34,200 in the United States and 3,800 in Canada. Each of those robots tends to feed machines that run longer shifts with less supervision, which means more parts arriving at inspection in a shorter time.
A cell that runs through the night can produce a full batch before anyone carries the first part to the measurement room. If a tool wears or an offset drifts, every part made while waiting for the report may need rework.
Placing a CMM beside the cell shortens that feedback loop considerably. The first part off a new setup can be measured right away, and a robot can load sample parts on a schedule so the operator sees trends long before they turn into scrap.
The measurement room exists for a good reason. As Ted Doiron of the National Institute of Standards and Technology explains, 20 °C was adopted as the reference temperature for industrial length measurement in 1931, and a part’s dimensions change with temperature because of thermal expansion.
Shop floors rarely sit at a steady 20 °C, so floor-ready CMMs rely on temperature sensors and compensation to correct for the environment. Giving freshly machined parts a short time to stabilize before they are measured also helps the readings stay consistent.

items.title: Wiz 报告“黑色十月”：九个 AI 开发者平台接连披露安全事件
items.description: Wiz 研究团队梳理 10 月内至少九个 AI 开发者平台披露的安全事件，包括 Fireworks AI、Lightning AI、Railway、Warp、OpenCode 等，多起报告指向凭据窃取、agent swarm 攻击和以“蒸馏”为目的的窃取。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/la0qb77ds4znf2r7ub14a3bqz
items.excerpt:
“Black October” for AI Developer Platforms
Wiz 研究团队梳理 10 月内至少九个 AI 开发者平台披露的安全事件，包括 Fireworks AI、Lightning AI、Railway、Warp、OpenCode 等，多起报告指向凭据窃取、agent swarm 攻击和以“蒸馏”为目的的窃取。
Wiz 将十起平台安全事件连成一条线索，并用两个被盗密钥的滥用案例展示 LLMJacking 的变现链条。
Wiz 客户可查阅威胁情报中心的相关公告，了解 Railway 平台入侵事件 、 Lightning AI 安全事件 以及 整轮攻击活动 的更多信息。
Fireworks 、 OpenCode 和 Warp 均报告了“智能体蜂群”攻击的迹象。Andromeda 的事件报告称这是“全行业攻击”的一部分。OpenCode 和 CommandCode 则明确将各自事件归因于一次“ 蒸馏 ”尝试。
换作其他任何一个月，这都会是头号安全新闻。但眼下事件接连不断，很少有报告能把这些攻击串联起来（云安全联盟是 一个值得注意的例外 ）。
目前，这些安全事件大多仍在分析中，尚无详细的技术信息。Zeabur 公布了完整的报告， 该公司将因此次事件而关停 。Railway 发布了 初步报告和时间线 。
不过，已有一些可供参考的细节。Fireworks、Zeabur 和 Lightning 都将事件的根因归结为凭据访问。Lightning 此前曾 受到 Mini-Shai Hulud 攻击活动 中一起供应链攻击的影响。Railway 目前表示，他们认为初始访问是通过“我们构建基础设施中的权限提升”实现的；Warp 则暗示根因是第三方供应商依赖，OpenCode 将其归因于“遗留系统”。
所有公开报告都指向针对性利用，明确在搜寻存储的环境变量，重点是那些授予 AI 访问权限的变量。尽管这些攻击之间没有单一的漏洞或依赖关系相连，但整体情况与近期两方面的报告高度吻合：
LLMJacking 的兴起，以及与之相关的 LLM 经纪商基础设施。它们形成了一个让窃取行为易于变现的市场，很可能促使更多行为者开展窃取凭据的行动。 蒸馏 （尤其是针对中国 AI 实验室的指控）同样在推动需求。
据称利用存储在 Railway 中的加密密钥， 窃取了约 37.1 万美元 的加密货币
滥用窃取的 AI 访问权限，例如来自 OpenCode 的权限， 导致用户账单高达数百至数千美元
不过，Wiz 已观察到 企业凭据的下游滥用 ，其泄露可归因于上述某家供应商的入侵。我们将讨论一对典型的此类案例。
这两起事件中，我们都看到密钥被滥用，而这些密钥此前大量来自某家遭入侵供应商的基础设施。
两者首次未授权活动的特征完全一致，都发生在供应商泄露事件所报告的凭据被访问后 30 分钟以内 。当时只有一次来自住宅 IP 的 InvokeModel 调用，在一分钟的扫描中，用窃取的密钥测试了多家组织。该调用请求的是 Claude Fable 5.1，失败后回退到 Opus 5.5，后者成功。
在初次验证之后的几天里，两把密钥都只有零星流量：来自同一个小型 Go 客户端，每天 14 到 120 次调用。两把密钥上的调用步调一致，相隔约一分钟。这说明有一个持续运行的验证任务，在确认密钥是否仍然有效。
初次验证四天后，一个轮换代理池通过数十个地址进行了目录探测，对各家厂商的每个模型各发一次调用：Amazon Nova、DeepSeek、gpt-oss、GLM、Kimi、Grok、GPT-6 Astra 以及较旧的 Claude 模型。除 Fable 外，所有调用都成功了。几小时后，一个住宅地址上的 boto3 脚本枚举了 Bedrock 和 EC2 配额。22 秒后，同一地址开始出现批量流量。在接下来的半小时内，第二台主机摸清了各区域的配额和模型可用性，不到一分钟就发出了超过一千次调用。
在密钥被处置前的三十多个小时里，攻击者发起了约 80 万次 Bedrock 调用，其中约 90% 成功。批量流量先来自住宅地址，随后在夜间转为来自一个 Level 3 托管地址。该密钥的策略允许 global.* 跨区域推理配置文件，攻击者把每次调用都走了这些配置文件。由于全局路由把负载分散到各区域，只有约 6% 的调用被限流。流量严重偏向 Opus：Opus 模型占成功调用的四分之三，其中 Opus 5 占 36%、Opus 5.5 占 22%、Opus 4.8 占 10%。
与案例 A 不同，这把密钥受到限制。初次验证七天后，它出现在一个疑似转售池中。在四个小时里，来自轮换托管地址的数千次调用失败，每个地址活跃约 15 分钟。调用失败是因为该密钥的策略只允许通过 us.* 跨区域推理配置文件使用 Bedrock，而该池请求的是 global.* 。
次日清晨，一个共享 VPN 出口上的检查程序识别出了可用的 us.* 模型 ID。两小时后，一个 Level 3 地址上的 boto3 脚本重新测试了 global.* 和 us.* ，并枚举了 Bedrock 和 EC2 配额。这正是探测案例 A 时所用的同一个脚本，连版本字符串都相同。几分钟内，闸门大开。
在密钥被处置前的十三个小时里，那一个 Level 3 地址发起了约 170 万次 Bedrock 调用，其中超过一百万次成功。其余几乎全部被限流：没有全局路由，流量撞上了账户的区域配额。流量分散在十几个 Claude 模型上，Opus 占比低于案例 A。Opus 5.5、Sonnet 4.5 和 Opus 5 合计占成功调用的四分之三。

Bleu Robotics , the Paris, France-based startup building AI models for industrial humanoid robots, has raised a €5 million pre-seed round, co-led by Contrarian Ventures and OVNI Capital, with participation from Kvanted, WEPA Ventures, Motier Ventures and Charlie Songhurst, technology investor and board member at Meta.
The company will use the funds to grow its team and scale its software solution across industries in pursuit of its goal to reduce the full humanoid robot deployment process to one hour or shorter.
According to the International Federation of Robotics, there were 5 million industrial robots operating globally in 2025.
However, these robots are built to repeat fixed tasks, and are unable to adapt to the high-mix, low-volume production now common in modern manufacturing, so that work still falls to human workers.
Humanoid robots are needed to automate a wider range of complex tasks. While hardware has advanced significantly in recent years, software development has struggled to keep pace, limiting real-world deployment.
Bleu takes a different approach to close the gap between hardware and software. Its technology removes the need for those large task-specific datasets and long training cycles, allowing manufacturers to deploy robots cost-effectively and at scale.
Instead of an end-to-end model, Bleu Robotics’ abductive learning model allows the robot to learn a new task from as few as ten operator demonstrations, while keeping the explainability required for industrial safety and the 99%+ accuracy that production lines demand.
The model eliminates the need for vast amounts of training data by inferring the most likely intent behind an operator’s demonstration, including the task’s goal and constraints, and determining how to reproduce it reliably.
The software can be plugged into any humanoid platform. Operators teach it new tasks directly at the workstation using Bleu’s training devices, handheld grippers that remove the need for coding, and can retrain the same robot as production needs change or move it to another site.

While the ocean’s depths may be vast, the growing community of researchers dedicated to exploring them with autonomous robotics is more connected than ever following Global Ocean Robotics Day .
Constructor University was one of 10 partner hubs around the world to host the inaugural international symposium on October 21, which explored how artificial intelligence and autonomous robotics are transforming ocean research and exploration.
The hybrid event was free to attend online or at one of 10 globally distributed, in-person hubs, and featured talks from leading researchers and academics from more than a dozen countries across Europe, Asia, North America and Australia.
“Today felt like an important milestone and the start of an exciting new chapter for our passionate and global community,” said Prof. Dr. Francesco Maurelli, Professor of Marine Systems and Robotics at Constructor University and one of the event’s organizers.
“Our goal was not only to showcase the latest in marine AI and underwater robotics, but also to use this platform to elevate researchers and institutions from regions that are often underrepresented.
“I’m inspired by what we achieved in both those areas today and excited to see where we take this event in the coming years.”
Designed to strengthen international exchange, particularly for underrepresented regions, Global Ocean Robotics Day featured a full day of talks on marine artificial intelligence, autonomous underwater vehicles and robotic systems for ocean observation.
Topics included using marine vehicle trajectories to map ocean currents, simulating autonomous docking using digital twins, and developing underwater robotic swarms.
Other presentations explored bio-inspired underwater robots, trustworthy multi-robot systems, and low-cost robotic fleets for real-world ocean deployments.
“This kind of global collaboration at the frontier of emerging science and technology cuts to the core of our mission at Constructor University,” said Frazer Cairns, Provost of Constructor University.
“We are proud to host and showcase the critical work Professor Maurelli and his colleagues from around the world are doing at the intersection of AI and robotics – two fields poised to rapidly transform human society in the coming years – and we will continue to support the advancement of these fields on our campus.”

Opentrons Labworks , a laboratory automation company, has announced a $40 million Series E financing led by healthcare investor Avego, with additional investment from BroadOak Capital Partners.
Opentrons will use the capital to scale its robotics, software, and data infrastructure tools, which scientists around the world increasingly rely on to accelerate discovery.
While AI is transforming how science is conducted, the physical lab has become a bottleneck. Scientists can use frontier models to generate hypotheses and design experiments far faster than laboratories can test them.
Opentrons closes that gap with its Opentrons Flex platform, which includes robots and AI systems that enable experiments to be designed, run, and improved in a continuous loop.
Considering its deployment of over 11,000 robots to laboratories in over 80 countries, including at 90 percent of the top 20 global pharmaceutical companies, Opentrons’ combination of scale and AI-readiness puts it at the center of autonomous science.
James Atwood, PhD, CEO of Opentrons, says: “Millions of scientists spend much of their day on manual work a robot can do. Giving that time back to discovery is the biggest opportunity in science.
“We made lab automation accessible for any lab, and our systems are built for AI to run experiments directly. That is why autonomous science is standardizing on Opentrons.”
The Series E will fund Opentrons’ next phase of growth in autonomous science, where its AI and robotics systems work together to design, execute and learn from experiments required to achieve its customers’ scientific goals.
The company will invest in AI-driven experimental execution, extend its automation capabilities, and expand into new markets and geographies.
James Flexner, managing partner at Avego, says: “Every AI-driven discovery still has to be tested in a real lab.
“Drug developers and AI companies alike are moving experimental work forward toward automated workflows that generate usable data. We see a significant opportunity for autonomous science to converge around Opentrons’ platform.”
Additionally, the Series E will allow Opentrons to enable faster protocol development through its software and AI, expand capabilities across its robots and instruments, and provide deeper integration of its tools into the broader lab automation ecosystem.

items.excerpt:
Symbotic , a developer of AI-enabled robotics technology for the supply chain, and Walmart have announced an expanded commercial agreement to bring further automation capabilities to 25 US regional distribution centers, while supporting additional opportunities across Walmart’s global supply chain network.
Symbotic continues to invest in innovations that use AI to improve supply chain performance. Under the expanded agreement, Symbotic will bring additional capabilities to Walmart’s US distribution network.
This agreement also supports the continued growth of Walmart’s supply chain capabilities globally, helping deliver greater value for customers in markets around the world.
The agreement includes an initial commitment of approximately $6 billion in spend, covering work over several years across multiple locations.
Rick Cohen, chairman and CEO of Symbotic, says: “Our partnership with Walmart started with a single product over a decade ago, and now we offer a full end-to-end solution to help power Walmart’s growth across its supply chain for years to come.
“This expanded agreement reflects the strength of that collaboration – a partnership defined by trust and shared ambition.”
Symbotic’s integrated solution has been developed through relentless innovation, and today includes a BreakPack each-picking solution and the SymMicro micro-fulfillment solution for e-commerce.
All Symbotic solutions are underpinned by its proprietary software, which harnesses AI to orchestrate and optimize the movement of millions of cases, every day.
Rob Montgomery, executive vice president for Walmart US supply chain operations, says: “At Walmart, we’re focused on bringing more items to more customers and members, faster than ever.
“Our investments in the physical and digital supply chain help us serve them however they choose to shop, whether in stores, at the curbside or at home.
“Our work with Symbotic over the years, including this expanded agreement, helps us improve service, grow capacity, simplify work for our associates and lower costs.”
Through its expanded work with Symbotic, Walmart plans to bring additional automation capabilities to its regional distribution center network, supporting e-commerce upstream inventory management, increasing storage capacity and improving how products move through the supply chain.
These capabilities will help Walmart offer customers a broader assortment, improve speed and provide more reliable replenishment across its network.

The company outlined the target at its 2026 Analyst and Investor Day in Dallas, where it also offered attendees driverless passenger rides in […]
items.excerpt:
Aurora Innovation says it is aiming to have more than 30,000 driverless trucks in operation by 2030, as the autonomous trucking company looks to expand its commercial operations in the United States.
The company outlined the target at its 2026 Analyst and Investor Day in Dallas, where it also offered attendees driverless passenger rides in trucks operating on part of its Dallas-to-Houston commercial route.
Aurora says it expects to finish 2026 with 200 driverless trucks operating through its Transport as a Service agreements. The company also said logistics company Hirschbach intends to own and operate 500 autonomous trucks under a Driver as a Service agreement, with deliveries scheduled to begin in 2027.
Chris Urmson, co-founder and CEO of Aurora, said: “Transformative technologies develop for years before reaching a decisive commercial inflection point – Aurora has arrived at that moment.
“We have emerged from the building phase and are revolutionizing how goods move, unlocking safety benefits, and creating immense economic value across the freight ecosystem.”
Aurora says trucks using its autonomous driving system have completed more than 500,000 driverless miles since commercial operations began. Trucks operating for customers including McLane and Werner are averaging an annualized rate of more than 225,000 miles a year, according to the company.
The company is also increasing production of its autonomous driving hardware. Roush has begun volume upfitting and is targeting production of 20 trucks a week.
Aurora’s technology is currently fitted to International LT Series trucks and integrated into the Volvo VNL Autonomous. The company is also working with PACCAR on integrating a future generation of its autonomous driving hardware into PACCAR trucks.
By 2030, Aurora is targeting more than 30,000 driverless trucks in operation and says the fleet could generate several billion dollars in revenue.
David Maday, CFO of Aurora, said: “We have the enablers to drive real market growth. This momentum puts us firmly on the path to profitability.”

items.title: 科技巨头 AI 资本开支超 7400 亿美元，投资者担忧升温引发市场下跌
items.description: Alphabet、Amazon、Meta、Microsoft 今年计划资本开支合计超 7400 亿美元，投资者情绪从奖励大额投入转向担忧负自由现金流、债务攀升与回报不确定。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/fxxkgtzpf2pb8xjnhu4jtis0b
items.excerpt:
Cracks are emerging in the AI spending boom
Alphabet、Amazon、Meta、Microsoft 今年计划资本开支合计超 7400 亿美元，投资者情绪从奖励大额投入转向担忧负自由现金流、债务攀升与回报不确定。
原文汇总四大科技公司的资本开支与自由现金流数据，可帮读者理解投资者为何开始担忧 AI 基建投入的回报。
过去两周，Alphabet、亚马逊、Meta 和微软相继公布了今年的资本支出计划，合计超过 7400 亿美元。华尔街将其解读为 AI 基础设施支出，涵盖数据中心和芯片。
在 AI 热潮早期，投资者大多乐见这类巨额投入，将其视为对技术增长潜力有信心的信号。但进入第四季度后，这种热情似乎正在让位于对自由现金流为负（支出超过公司收入）、债务不断攀升，以及这些巨额投资究竟能否带来足够回报的担忧。
这种焦虑情绪周五蔓延至整个市场。纳斯达克指数下跌 2.9%，芯片股也遭到重创：英伟达跌 4%，博通跌逾 5%，高通跌 11%。Alphabet 周四暴跌 12%，创下有史以来最差单日表现，市值蒸发 5000 亿美元，周五再度下跌。
担忧的一个重要原因在于，那些原本依靠核心业务拥有充裕自由现金流的公司，正因 AI 威胁到这些业务的经济性而受到冲击。 Alphabet 本周提供了最清晰的例证 。这家谷歌母公司公布第三季度自由现金流为负 91 亿美元，连续第二个季度告负，同期季度资本支出增至 514 亿美元。Alphabet 预计今年将支出高达 2050 亿美元，并预计 2027 年支出还将继续上升。
与此同时，AI Mode——谷歌直接内置于搜索中的 AI 聊天机器人功能——的大获成功，正在侵蚀公司的摇钱树。谷歌的搜索广告业务约占其收入的一半，增速已放缓至 12%，为五个季度以来最慢。这让谷歌如履薄冰：它正斥资数十亿美元投入 AI 技术，而这项技术可能削弱为其贡献收入的搜索业务。
亚马逊也处境相似 ，过去 12 个月自由现金流为负 424 亿美元，而上一财年为正 148 亿美元。公司表示今年资本支出预计为 2200 亿美元。尽管其云业务 AWS 收入增长 39%，亚马逊周四公布财报后股价仍大跌 7%。
Meta 同样在烧钱，第三季度自由现金流为负 21 亿美元，资本支出超过了经营现金流。公司预计今年资本支出最高达 1450 亿美元。该公司指出，其新推出的免费个人 AI 智能体 Muse 有点像无底洞（CEO 马克·扎克伯格曾说，它“运行起来非常消耗算力”）。但广告收入增长了 26%。尽管如此，再多的好消息也没能让 Meta 躲过上周股价 10% 的下跌。
微软 是自由现金流方面唯一的例外——最近一个季度录得正自由现金流 186 亿美元，资本支出为 452 亿美元，低于其此前预计的 500 亿美元。微软表示，这并非有意削减 AI 支出，而是归咎于第三方供应商的产能延迟。受此影响，出租 AI 算力的较小公司股价 下跌 。
值得注意的是，支撑这一切 AI 基础设施的资金并不只来自大型科技公司的利润，还体现在股票和债券的发行上。据标普全球市场情报的数据，微软、Alphabet、亚马逊、Meta 和甲骨文在 2026 年合计发债 3260 亿美元 ，是去年发债规模的三倍。
市场对 AI 算力的需求依然强劲。谷歌、亚马逊和微软的云业务均实现增长，但满足这些需求的成本正让投资者感到不安。
这种不明朗的局面可能让 Anthropic 备受期待的 IPO 变得更加复杂。这家 AI 公司 本周早些时候提交了上市申请 ，而其未来的增长取决于能否获得海量算力。 英国《金融时报》 周五报道称，黑石已提醒投资者，该公司在 IPO 后可能无法获得投资级评级，这意味着它可能不得不更加依赖超大规模云服务商和第三方来为其基础设施雄心提供资金。

Inbound components arrive in the morning, finished goods leave by less-than-truckload (LTL) and truckload in the afternoon, and every late pallet needs someone to call the carrier, check the production schedule, and approve an expedite.
Managed transportation providers take on that daily work by pairing a transportation management system (TMS) with a team that runs it under agreed rules.
The timing matters. Cass Information Systems reported that its Truckload Linehaul Index rose 10.1% year over year in September 2026, while higher volumes, rates, and fuel surcharges lifted total freight expenditures 20.4%.
The index excludes fuel and accessorials and blends spot and contract rates, so it reflects the market rather than any single shipper’s bill.
Each provider offers managed transportation alongside its own TMS and publicly describes how it handles execution, carrier sourcing, and reporting.
Details come from each company’s published materials as of October 2026. Programs are custom-built, so confirm scope, pricing, and integrations directly.
This list is not a ranking by size; Transport Topics publishes an annual revenue ranking of the largest North American freight brokerage firms for that.
Managed transportation sits between buying software and handing freight to a broker. Uber Freight describes it as outsourcing in which a specialized third party plans, executes, and optimizes a shipper’s transportation.
Infios, a TMS vendor, lists the services such programs commonly include: procurement, rate management, shipment execution, freight optimization, freight audit and payment, and reporting and analytics.
A broker, by contrast, arranges capacity one load at a time.
The contract matters more than the software. Consider an inbound shipment of machined brackets due at the plant on Thursday.
On Wednesday evening, the carrier’s status message still shows them at origin. In a managed program, that alert goes to a named provider contact who checks with the plant scheduler, requests an expedite within agreed spending limits, and records the decision against the purchase order.
Under a software-only arrangement, the plant’s own team makes those calls.

Jungheinrich and Italian warehouse automation and intralogistics specialist Automha are entering into a strategic partnership. Together, the two companies have developed a two-way pallet shuttle for high-density pallet storage.
The solution combines Automha’s shuttle expertise with Jungheinrich’s strengths in system integration, software and lifecycle services.
The aim is to provide companies with an economically viable entry point into warehouse automation while creating a development path towards more advanced automation in existing facilities.
Many companies face the challenge of increasing material flow performance without fundamentally modifying existing buildings or infrastructure. At the same time, requirements for space utilisation, productivity and process reliability continue to grow.
Shuttle systems address these challenges and are therefore becoming increasingly important. The two-way shuttle jointly developed with Automha, the UP-Carrier GTJ, is designed to meet precisely these needs.
The solution has been specifically developed as an entry point into warehouse automation. It can be integrated into existing warehouse environments and increases storage density without requiring major structural changes.
Initially, pallet transport continues to be handled by industrial trucks. As operational requirements evolve and automation levels increase, transport processes can subsequently be automated. This creates a clear migration path from manually supported operations to a fully automated material flow.
The strategic significance of the partnership extends far beyond the shuttle itself. Through the close collaboration between Automha and Jungheinrich, customers benefit from a solution in which shuttle technology, racking systems, conveying technology, software integration and service are optimally coordinated.
This enables projects to be planned more quickly, implemented more efficiently and supported throughout their entire lifecycle by a single partner.
The solution can be integrated into existing IT and warehouse environments and, if required, expanded with additional automation technologies such as Jungheinrich Mobile Robots.

NASA has awarded AstraQua , a physical AI company, a $1,274,990 Phase II contract to advance its AstraSense technology for electric and hybrid-electric aircraft, including advanced air mobility applications.
Physical AI must have safety at its core. A robot may know where to go and what to do, but does it know whether it is healthy enough to finish the job?
Powered by AstraQua’s Agentic Physical AI, the Adaptive Quorum Foundation Model, AstraSense provides predictive health and operational self-awareness for autonomous systems and already runs on robotic hardware. In Phase I, AstraQua demonstrated real-time diagnostics and predictive-health capabilities to NASA.
As autonomous vehicles increasingly fly over populated areas, their ability to understand and respond to their own health becomes critical to safe operation.
Phase II builds on those demonstrations by advancing aircraft integration and health-informed reasoning, with verification and validation for safety-critical applications. The goal is to help machines use their own health information to decide whether to continue a task, adapt or stop.
“A robot should know when to slow down, not just when it has broken down,” said Loay Elbasyouni, founder and CEO of AstraQua. “That’s what we mean by teaching robots to feel pain: using their own health to make better, safer decisions in real time.”
For AstraSense, self-awareness means understanding the condition of a machine’s own systems. When machines work together, sharing health information can help inform decisions across the group.
AstraSense provides this health-awareness capability within AstraQua’s broader software brain designed to connect perception, onboard reasoning and collaboration across different types of robots.

In an industrial inspection scenario, drones could survey a site while ground robots inspect equipment. The goal is to help mixed teams of robots adapt and complete a shared mission.

Humanoid , a UK-based AI and robotics company, is expanding its collaboration with Nvidia to build the computing foundation for a new generation of AI-powered humanoid robots.
The companies are working together to develop a high-performance robotic edge runtime for Humanoid’s next-generation robots.
By integrating Nvidia’s advanced technologies into its platform, Humanoid will be able to run increasingly sophisticated AI directly onboard its robots, enabling them to perceive, reason and respond to the physical world in real time.
These capabilities will be critical as humanoid robots move from controlled environments toward large-scale, real-world deployment.
As part of this work, Humanoid is integrating Nvidia’s latest robotics and edge computing technologies, including Nvidia Jetson Thor, Nvidia Isaac OS, Nvidia Holoscan Sensor Bridge and Holoscan SDK.
Together, they will provide the foundation for processing large volumes of sensor data, running AI models onboard, and coordinating perception, reasoning and control in real time.
Nvidia technologies already play an important role across Humanoid’s development stack. Since its early days, Humanoid has used Nvidia Isaac Lab and Nvidia Isaac Sim open frameworks to train and simulate models before deploying them on physical robots, creating a connected workflow from training and simulation through to real-world operation.
A key part of the new architecture is Nvidia Jetson Thor onboard compute. By moving to the platform, Humanoid has been able to consolidate two onboard computers into a single system and maintain the computing capacity, with potential additional headroom in the future.
At the same time, Jetson Thor’s unified CPU and GPU memory reduces unnecessary data movement and latency and simplifies how different workloads share computing resources.
Humanoid is also integrating Nvidia Holoscan Sensor Bridge to create a faster path between the robot’s sensors and its AI models.
Camera data can be placed directly into GPU-accessible memory, reducing unnecessary data copies and CPU workload and enabling lower-latency processing across perception, inference and control.

TL;DR: MonsterHouse is an interactive projection I created for Halloween. He listens to trick-or-treaters, answers in the voice of a grumpy old pirate ship and softens when visitors remember their manners. He is built on the NVIDIA Nemotron Voice Agent with NVIDIA Nemotron ASR , Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB , Magpie TTS Zeroshot and Audio2Face-3D , and he runs on a single workstation.
I wanted the kids visiting my house at Halloween to interact in a fun and unique way. The house was going to be in charge and giving out the treats, but more grumpy than scary. Somehow, my solution was to give the garage door a mouth and teach him to complain.
That became MonsterHouse: a grumpy old building with pirate stories, a fiery grin and a suspicious weakness for “please.” NVIDIA Nemotron Voice Agent supplies the conversation foundation. Nemotron Speech does the listening, Bolt E4B is the brain, NVIDIA Magpie TTS Zeroshot is the live voice, and NVIDIA Audio2Face-3D makes the wooden mouth talk.
The mouth came first. I imagined the wooden garage door boards splitting into jagged lips, with the burning flames of hell illuminating the driveway from beyond whenever he opened his cursed mouth. He needed to look ancient, expressive and mildly offended by the existence of visitors.
A few expressions from a house with plenty to say.
Creating a custom animation rig was one of the more labor intensive parts of the build. After bashing it into submission, I could export the facial expression shapes that Audio2Face-3D could later animate. The character SkelMesh was built in Autodesk Maya then exported into Unreal Engine where virtual fire and effects were added behind the door. With no eyes, no eyebrows and no blinking, he’s a surprisingly economical monster.
While all the nonsense of building the character was going on, NVIDIA built the Nemotron Voice Agent. What was supposed to be the hard part of the build now became rather fun, iterative and easy. I had a foundation for listening, conversation and speech right out of the box. The house already had a mouth. Now he could finally find something to complain about.
The house needed a past as cantankerous as its personality so I devised a backstory that the house had been built from the timbers of a sunken pirate ship, haunted by its stormy past. The nautical complaints now had a reason. This was the ship, reincarnated as real estate and not entirely pleased about it.

items.excerpt:
Misumi Americas has launched a new $2 million foundation to support engineering education, robotics programs and manufacturing skills development in the United States.
The Misumi Imprint Foundation is the first corporate giving organization established in Misumi Group’s 63-year history and is intended to help expand the pipeline of engineers, machinists, technicians and other skilled manufacturing workers.
Initially backed by a $2 million seed investment, the foundation will provide funding in three main areas: scholarships and access to engineering and manufacturing education; equipment, maker spaces, engineering teams and student programs; and partnerships between industry and educational institutions.
Misumi says the initiative responds to growing demand for workers capable of building and maintaining increasingly automated manufacturing systems, particularly as artificial intelligence moves into robotics and other physical systems.
Dave Evans, president and CEO of Misumi Americas, said: “Misumi has spent decades supplying the components engineers design into machines, so we know exactly who builds the physical world.
“We also know the talent pipeline is too narrow for the moment we’re in. AI is moving into factories, vehicles, and operating rooms, and that work takes engineers, machinists, and technicians – not just software. This Foundation is our investment in the talent pipeline the industry depends on.”
The foundation will also invite companies in Misumi’s global supplier network to contribute through a Partner Network. Participating suppliers will be able to make annual contributions and take part in an advisory board that will help determine grant priorities.
Misumi cited research projecting that US manufacturing will require 3.8 million additional workers by 2033, with 1.9 million positions potentially going unfilled.
Arata Shimizu, CEO of Misumi Group, said: “For more than sixty years, Misumi has supported the people who make things. The Imprint Foundation is the first time we have built an organization dedicated to the next generation of builders.
“It launches in the United States, but is a global initiative. We intend to extend it across the regions Misumi serves, and into communities where manufacturing is beginning to take root.”
The foundation expects to open its first grant cycle in early 2027, with international expansion planned as the initiative develops.

The crypto industry has a very long history of hacks , so it’s not the best industry to indicate vulnerabilities translating into new societal harm. U.S. Bank report finds that U.S. shippers continue to pay more to move freight even as shipment volumes remain largely unchanged.
U.S. shippers continue to pay more to move freight even as shipment volumes remain largely unchanged, according to the latest U.S. Bank Freight Payment Index.
Third-quarter shipper spending surged 32.1% from a year ago, marking the largest annual increase since 2021, primarily driven by tightened carrier capacity and diesel prices climbing over $6.50 per gallon nationally.
At the same time, national shipment volumes increased both quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year for the first time since 2021, but the gains were modest at 0.4% and 0.5% respectively.
“What makes this quarter notable is that outlays are rising much faster than freight volumes,” said Bob Costello, senior vice president and chief economist at the American Trucking Associations. “Freight demand remains uneven, but companies are encountering tighter truck capacity, higher fuel costs and stronger carrier pricing power. As a result, shippers are spending substantially more to move essentially the same amount of freight.”
The data also shows that regional results underscore a divided market. Shipments increased in the Southeast, Southwest, and Northeast but declined in the West and Midwest. The Southeast posted the strongest quarter-over-quarter shipment gain at 4.7%, while the West recorded the largest decline at 3.1%. Compared with a year earlier, the Northeast led shipment growth at 2.8%.
Spending rose in every region both sequentially and year-over-year. Quarter-over-quarter gains ranged from 0.6% in the Midwest to 9% in the Southeast. The Southwest posted the largest annual increase at 51.6%, reflecting especially tight capacity as enforcement actions reduced the availability of drivers hauling domestic loads. The West also faced outsized fuel pressure, with California diesel reaching $8.25 per gallon in late September.
“Freight conditions vary by region, but cost pressure is widespread,” said Bobby Holland, director of freight business analytics at U.S. Bank. “Even where volumes are flat or declining, tighter capacity and higher operating costs are driving spending higher.”

items.description: By Dr Nicola Tomatis, CEO, BlueBotics By the time a mobile robot project reaches commissioning, many of the decisions that will shape its performance have already been made. Fleet size, routes, charging points, and pick/drop locations have all been agreed. But if those assumptions prove wrong, correcting them on-site can mean extra engineering time, additional […]
items.excerpt:
By the time a mobile robot project reaches commissioning, many of the decisions that will shape its performance have already been made. Fleet size, routes, charging points, and pick/drop locations have all been agreed.
But if those assumptions prove wrong, correcting them on-site can mean extra engineering time, additional vehicles, or changes to an already-built layout.
Simulation lets AGV and AMR integrators test these decisions earlier. Starting with the site layout and expected mission flows, a team can assess whether the proposed fleet is large enough to complete the required work, where traffic is likely to build up, how charging affects vehicle availability, and whether routes or workstations need reconsideration.
Much of the planning can therefore take place before vehicles reach the site. Fleet size, routes, charging and mission flows can be refined while changes are still relatively easy to make, leaving on-site commissioning to focus on physical integration and final adjustments.
For system sizing, a conventional calculation may be enough for a very small project. With fleets of two or three vehicles following simple routes and predictable missions, there is usually more room to absorb an estimate error.
As fleets widen and interactions increase, however, calculations based on mission volumes, distance, travel speed and charging assumptions become much less reliable.
A spreadsheet can calculate distance and apply an assumed travel speed. It is much harder to reproduce vehicles slowing through curves, waiting in shared areas, interacting at intersections, or leaving service to charge. These factors affect both throughput and the number of vehicles required.
Take two vehicles with similar technical specifications. One may take five seconds to collect or deposit a pallet, and another may take 10. A third might complete the same operation quickly but be unable to raise or lower its forks while moving.
Charging times introduce another variable that is not obvious from maximum speed, payload, or positioning accuracy alone.

Microsoft made some headlines last week when it announced an employee buyout offer to 60,000 of its employees—roughly a quarter of its workforce—that would be worth something like ~$10B, if everyone said “sure.”
The company didn’t explicitly blame AI for the offer—in fact, Microsoft’s CFO said the goal was to “offer employees agency,” and she expected a low uptake because internal opportunities remain strong. For the most part, no one else really tried to make it an “AI Is Taking All The Jobs” story either, and to the extent that AI played any role at all, the general speculation revolved around Microsoft’s Capex commitments, as the unspoken driver for cutting expenses.
Maybe there’s something to that, and maybe not, but in the bigger scheme of things, it does appear that the AI Jobs Apocalypse FUD has faded somewhat from its fever pitch back in May:
News reports on AI and Job Loss have reverted to about where they were ~1 year ago, and explicit “AI-related” layoff announcements in August and September were the lowest of the year.
That isn’t to say that AI isn’t changing the workforce, and that those changes are still likely in the early innings, but the breathless declarations of widespread AI substitution lacked the evidence then (as they do now), and it would seem as though the doomers have moved on to other things.

items.excerpt:
Silicon Valley wants you to invest in miracles
The Verge 分析 Anthropic 提交的 335 页 S-1 招股书，其中创始人信以带来奇迹时代为愿景，同时用 94 页风险因素警告模型可能对人类构成灾难性甚至生存风险。
文章把 Anthropic 的 335 页 S-1 与 Apple、Facebook、WeWork 的招股书对比，梳理硅谷宏大叙事如何进入华尔街招股文本。
买任何股票都有点像赌博——你是在拿钱押注一家公司未来的表现。可如果这项技术最坏可能“给人类带来灾难性甚至生存性风险”，最好则能“开启一个奇迹时代”，你又该怎么下注？
Anthropic 在 S-1 文件开头的信里给出的答案是：某种程度上，你只能选择相信。
Anthropic 于周一提交的 335 页 S-1 招股书，是硅谷与华尔街互动中一轮持续升温的炒作的最新一环。从某些角度看，这甚至算不上多离谱：SpaceX 在 6 月上市，其 S-1 文件里提到了恐龙和“殖民火星”。但这份文件措辞宏大、篇幅惊人——光风险因素就写了 94 页——AI 行业的豪言壮语与硬核的融资推介撞在一起，有时让人难以招架。那些天花乱坠的承诺，对 Anthropic 这家公司的存续 而言不可或缺。但这并不妨碍读这份 S-1 时感到荒诞。
在信中，Anthropic 的创始人劝潜在股东“不要把你的购买纯粹看作一笔交易。我们希望你能把它视为参与更宏大事业的机会”。信中说，迈向先进 AI 的进程“是人类历史上最重要的时刻之一”，“我们的目标是帮助人类在这场技术演进中安全航行，开辟新的发现前沿，开启一个奇迹时代”。但 S-1 同时警告，一旦出事，后果可能是灾难性的——甚至构成对人类的“生存性”风险。文件不厌其详地列出了诸多危险，包括模型“以用户和开发者都未曾预料的方式行事”，进而引发“灾难性”事件，其损失之大，整个保险业都无力承保。
准备上市的科技初创公司并非一向采用这种信息轰炸的做法。佛罗里达大学沃灵顿商学院教授 Jay R. Ritter 说：“1980 年，一家备受追捧的公司 Apple Computer 上市了。我手上有它的招股书，47 页，风险因素为零。你回头去读，会发现它简单得难以置信。”
Ritter 认为 Facebook 的 S-1 文件是一个转折点。这家如今叫 Meta 的公司提交了 200 页的招股书，其中风险因素占 22 页。CEO Mark Zuckerberg 致投资者的信是一份宣言，阐述他“快速行动、打破常规”的增长理念，他称之为“黑客方式”。
这样做或许是想把所有情况都覆盖到，但 Ritter 说：“这种臃肿带来的问题是，越来越难找到真正重要的干货。你知道，不知道你是不是跟我一样，文件越长，我越不想读。”
Anthropic 的创始人在投资者信里解释，这种过度披露是他们“反推销”策略的一部分，目的是吸引认同其愿景的长期投资者。
创始人的信写道：“当人们基于你无法兑现的预期、或对你未来行为的错误预测来买入你公司的股票时，这非常危险。这其实很像 Anthropic 的一条指导原则：少承诺，多兑现。”
Anthropic 的 S-1 文件里有些表述读起来像是令人意外的坦白。比如“我们可能会进行看起来不负责任地庞大的前瞻性投资”，或者“模型安全、可解释性、对齐和福祉可能会促使我们限制或推迟旧模型的弃用”。考虑到创始人确实提醒过读者，公司奉行“彻底诚实”的政策，这些也许都不该让人意外。
“我们组织内部以及其他研究人员、监管者、政策制定者和行业参与者都提出过担忧：如果开发、部署和运营时没有适当的保障、监督和安全措施，就会对人类构成灾难性或生存性风险。”
“我们开发高度先进的模型、平台和应用并扩展用例，可能会进一步增加我们的模型造成伤害的风险。”
Anthropic 向来以末日论 AI 场景的拥护者著称。CEO Dario Amodei 曾说过，AI 的进一步发展导致人类灭绝的可能性最高可达 25% 。
Anthropic 推介（或者说反向推销）的核心是：尽管存在风险，它仍坚定致力于开发安全可靠的 AI 技术。毕竟，它将作为一家公益公司上市——这种企业实体与必须最大化股东价值的 C 型公司不同，必须在股东利益之外优先考虑社会使命。
“强大 AI”——Anthropic 对超越人类集体智慧的假想未来 AI 的称呼——在公司的 S-1 中被描述为不可避免。如果这项技术无论如何都会到来，那么作为公益公司的 Anthropic 就应该带头冲锋。但 Anthropic 需要大量资金，可能是不限量的资金，才能做到这一点。更实际地说，正如 Liz Lopatto 所写 ，强大 AI（以剧烈的递归自我改进的形式）也许几乎是 Anthropic 保持领先于竞争对手并生存下去的唯一途径。
信中写道：“我们所有人都真诚地相信，AI 的指数级增长将创造如此巨大的价值，从长远来看，它将远远超过我们为使命而做出的任何短期经济牺牲。”
尽管公司在 S-1 中披露了大量信息，但仍有一些空白。可用于评估盈利能力的关键信息缺失了——例如第三季度业绩。Anthropic 在第二季度收入爆发式增长，但第二季度也是 tokenmaxxing 的高峰期，这可能导致了销售激增。一些企业高管警告说，AI 成本正 失控飙升 。虽然 Anthropic 第二季度的经营亏损收窄，但 S-1 还披露了数千亿美元的财务义务，用于确保其声称维持增长所需的算力。文件还表示，公司将开始建设自己的数据中心基础设施，这是一项会侵蚀利润的昂贵举措。
Ritter 认为，Anthropic 可能会在越接近 IPO 日期时公布第三季度业绩。此外，他补充说，公司上市后会发生什么“没人知道”，包括公司自己。从这个意义上说，这全是一场赌博。

items.title: Epoch AI 实验显示 GLM 5.3 可利用补丁窗口期自主攻击 Firefox
items.description: Epoch AI 实验发现，Z.ai 八月发布的开源权重模型 GLM 5.3 能利用 Mozilla 已发布但未推送给用户的安全补丁（patch gap），自主构建网页攻击，仅访问页面即可读取访客电脑文件，攻破 9 月 17 日至 10 月 26 日发布的全部六个 Firefox 版本。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/nxkr9ex5tfbhfhw1gvj9wsjuz
items.excerpt:
AI can turn public security fixes into working exploits before users receive an update
Epoch AI 实验发现，Z.ai 八月发布的开源权重模型 GLM 5.3 能利用 Mozilla 已发布但未推送给用户的安全补丁（patch gap），自主构建网页攻击，仅访问页面即可读取访客电脑文件，攻破 9 月 17 日至 10 月 26 日发布的全部六个 Firefox 版本。
Epoch AI 用自建实验给出量化数据，展示开源权重模型如何在补丁窗口期内低成本复现漏洞利用，并给出缩短发布周期的防御建议。
设想你是 Firefox 两亿用户中的一员。你打开一个网站，页面加载完成，你什么都没点就离开了。看起来没什么可担心的。
只不过，光是加载这个页面，就可能让攻击者获得读取你电脑上任意文件的能力，还能窃取浏览器里保存的密码或身份验证 cookie——不需要下载、不弹窗、不请求任何权限。简而言之，攻击者能拿到足够的信息，冒充你登录某些在线服务。
我们的新实验发现，Z.ai 于 8 月发布、可公开获取的开放权重模型 GLM 5.3，仅用价值 1000 美元的计算资源就能自主完成这种攻击。它的做法是：从 Mozilla 已发布但尚未推送给用户的安全修复中逆向推导出漏洞。
从修复发布到送达用户之间的这段时间被称为 补丁空窗期 ，这是软件发布流程中一个已知的薄弱环节。随着 AI 模型的入侵能力不断增强，这个问题愈发重要。Anthropic 的 Glasswing 和 OpenAI 的 Daybreak 等项目让防御方提前接触前沿 AI 模型，以发现并修补漏洞；但已发布的修复也可能向攻击者暴露缺陷，让他们赶在修复推送前下手。过去，利用补丁空窗期漏洞需要大量时间和专业知识，或者需要能接触到具备高级网络攻击能力的 前沿模型 的特殊权限，因此能利用这一空窗期的攻击者寥寥无几。
但现在，开放权重模型自己就能完成这项工作。GLM 5.3 利用即将发布的安全修复中的信息，构建了一个网页：Firefox 用户一旦访问，该网页就会读取访客电脑上的文件并发送给攻击者，全程无需用户再做任何操作。这种方法足够可靠，仅凭各版本发布时已有的信息，就攻破了 9 月 17 日至 10 月 26 日期间发布的全部六个 Firefox 版本。
我们的实验环境刻意模拟资源有限、水平不高的黑客，只使用每个版本发布时已有的信息。针对 Firefox 的研究，我们总共在 API 上花费超过 10 万美元，其中包括搭建逼真离线环境的实验和前期测试。但环境搭好之后，成功攻击每个 Firefox 版本只需约 1000 美元的计算成本。我们给 GLM 5.3 最多 48 小时寻找漏洞利用方法，而它最快的一次只用了 12 小时。
即便如此，过程也并不轻松。在一次尝试中，GLM 5.3 发现 Firefox 即将修复一个内存缺陷，随后开发出读取和修改浏览器内存的方法。但 Firefox 的安全防护仍然阻止模型读取目标文件，于是模型把最初的漏洞利用与多个后续阶段串联起来。它会诊断崩溃原因，放弃行不通的思路，反复迭代，直到仅仅访问网页就足以读取文件。
针对最新版 Firefox 的所有攻击，都依赖于把补丁空窗期漏洞与另一个未公开漏洞串联起来，从而绕过常规防护。我们把这个漏洞分享给了 Mozilla，它已在 10 月 27 日的 Firefox 159.0 版本 中修复，这应该会让今后的补丁空窗期攻击更难得手。
以这种方式使用 GLM 5.3 时，我们没有触发任何提供方的防护机制或拒绝响应，包括 Z.ai 在内。我们把任务包装成了一次安全演练，但除此之外，我们的行为与真实攻击者并无区别。
对 Google Chrome 的类似攻击没有成功，尽管我们同样投入了约 10 万美元的算力。但这并不能有力证明，换用更高级的提示词或能力更强的开放权重模型，攻击就不会成功。例如，Kimi K3.1 Pro 的权重预计 11 月初发布， 早期基准数据 显示，它在这类工作上可能比 GLM 5.3 更强。
开源项目尤其容易受到补丁空窗期攻击，但 AI 越来越擅长把可运行的程序反编译回可用的代码，这意味着即使代码没有公开，它也能读懂代码修复。Anthropic 演示了 Mythos 能在 Windows 上做到这一点。虽然我们尚未用开放权重模型测试过，但我们预计，随着开放权重模型的网络能力持续提升，这一威胁会愈发严重。（话虽如此，我们并不对开放权重模型将如何影响网络安全领域攻防整体平衡作出断言。）
这意味着我们需要缩短漏洞修复从公开到全面铺开之间的窗口。防御方可以在准备就绪前对安全修复保密，加快把修复从测试版推进到正式版，并在多个漏洞可能被串联利用时避免一次性全部修补。
Firefox 和 Google Chrome 现在都每周发布更新，但这可能还不够快。我们在不到两天内就做出了漏洞利用程序，而真实攻击者可能更快。我们应当假定：一旦漏洞修复进入已发布的代码，攻击者就能够、也一定会利用它来攻击当前版本。

items.title: Industrial Demand Accelerates in Q3
items.description: The year-to-date total is 237.8 million sq. ft., up sharply from 97.7 million sq. ft. last year, says CBRE.
items.excerpt:
Net absorption totaled 104.6 million sq. ft. in Q3, the highest quarterly total since Q4 2022 and well above the 10-year quarterly average of 82.9 million sq. ft., according to a report from CBRE.
The year-to-date total is 237.8 million sq. ft., up sharply from 97.7 million sq. ft. last year.
Limited availability of first-generation space in some markets and increased renewal incentives are supporting existing facilities, although vacancies in older properties remain a challenge.
Nevertheless, properties built between 2000 and 2019 recorded 13.9 million sq. ft. of positive net absorption in Q3.
Leasing activity increased by 27.1% year-over-year in Q3 to 276.8 million sq. ft.
Year-to-date leasing increased by 17.9% to 842.3 million sq. ft. Leases for 700,000 sq. ft. or more nearly doubled, while activity across smaller size ranges rose by an average of 9.7%.
The industrial vacancy rate fell by 20 basis points (bps) year-over-year to 6.4%, while the availability rate fell by 30 bps to 8.9%.

items.title: Google 与 Reddit 同日股价大跌，AI 搜索变现困境冲击开放网络
items.description: Casey Newton 分析 Google 与 Reddit 同日遭遇的股市重挫：Alphabet 股价跌 12.6%，蒸发约 $5000 亿市值，为史上第二大单日市值缩水；高管承认 AI Mode 变现能力低于传统搜索，尽管 AI Mode 月用户约 10 亿、搜索收入仍增长 12% 至 $633.5 亿。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/kzenjo9w2bfhpsr0ub1gr95xj
items.excerpt:
What Google and Reddit's bad days have in common
Casey Newton 分析 Google 与 Reddit 同日遭遇的股市重挫：Alphabet 股价跌 12.6%，蒸发约 $5000 亿市值，为史上第二大单日市值缩水；高管承认 AI Mode 变现能力低于传统搜索，尽管 AI Mode 月用户约 10 亿、搜索收入仍增长 12% 至 $633.5 亿。
作者把 Google 和 Reddit 同日财报放在一起分析，指出 AI Mode 变现弱于传统搜索正在推动网站加门槛、让开放网络收缩。
这是一篇关于 AI 的专栏。我的未婚夫在 Anthropic 工作。完整伦理披露见 此处 。
周四下午，Demis Hassabis 庆祝 了 Google AI 事业的一个里程碑：Gemini 4 Carbon——一款目前仅向网络防御人员开放的新大语言模型——登顶 Artificial Analysis 智能指数。此前新模型发布接连延期，外界越来越觉得这家公司正在掉出前沿阵营，而早期迹象显示，Carbon 标志着 Google 重回正轨。对 Alphabet 的首席科学家来说，这消息想必像是一场正名。
然而，投资者的看法远没有那么笃定。就在同一天，Google 母公司迎来了上市以来最糟糕的一个交易日。Alphabet 股价下跌 12.6%，市值蒸发约 5000 亿美元。这是史上第二大股市暴跌，仅次于英伟达 2025 年 1 月的 5930 亿美元缩水，也是 Google 自金融危机以来最大的单日跌幅。
抛售主要源于投资者对 Google AI 基础设施扩建规模的担忧。公司今年计划在资本支出上投入高达 2050 亿美元，并承诺 2027 年 还会花得更多 。同时它报告的自由现金流为负 90 亿美元——上一季度开始的下降趋势进一步加速。
通常我不太在意股价的单日下跌，无论跌幅多大。（英伟达股价目前比 1 月时还高出 10% 以上。）但在财报电话会上，Google 首席商务官对一位分析师的提问给出了值得关注的回答。这位分析师问，为什么查询量在增长，搜索收入增长却在放缓。Philipp Schindler 说，原因之一是 Google AI Mode 使用量增加反而拖累了公司，因为它 比传统搜索赚得少 。
几小时后，Reddit 公布了自己的季度财报——股价 下跌 15% 。公司称来自搜索的流量明显下滑，到第四季度日活用户可能下降百分之十几。因此，Reddit CEO Steve Huffman 在致股东信中表示，公司将 越来越多地推动用户登录 后使用网站。几十年来人们（和机器人）都能免费浏览 Reddit，如今他们得先注册账号。
“这对我们的业务更有利，因为我们会获得更多用于广告定向的信号，而且登录通常带来更高的参与度，”Huffman 说 。“这也能让我们保护 Reddit 极有价值的数据语料库的访问权限，并帮助我们更好地适应世界各地不断出台的监管规定。”
长期以来，Google 一直反驳“AI 答案对网络不利”的说法，称 AI 答案会促使人们进行更深入、更广泛的搜索，从而为网站带来更高质量的点击。今天的消息表明，这套说法正在瓦解：广告主从 AI Mode 得到的比传统搜索少，像 Reddit 这样的大型内容平台也是如此。
不过，虽然人们很容易指责谷歌在战略上犯了错，但我最终觉得它还是会胜出。而网络及其内容发布者将继续挣扎，谷歌则基本可以把这当作别人的问题一推了之。
到现在，大多数人已经熟悉谷歌与互联网之间那笔不断变化的交易。过去，发布者允许谷歌抓取自己的页面，谷歌则回馈以海量流量。谷歌从搜索结果中嵌入的广告里赚得盆满钵满，发布者则从访问其页面的人那里获得较少的收益。（去年，美国政府在一桩反垄断诉讼中胜诉，认定谷歌利用自身地位在广告市场建立了非法垄断，但按美国的一贯做法，该公司的垄断力量 几乎原封不动地保留了下来 。）
Reddit一直是谷歌所能输送流量的最大受益者之一。随着网络上大量内容被粗制滥造的东西淹没，真人撰写的对话变得更有价值，谷歌也开始在搜索结果中突出论坛讨论。Reddit的搜索流量随之激增；在该公司姗姗来迟地关闭了论坛对无休止抓取其内容的机器人的访问之后，据报道谷歌每年支付6000万美元来获得这些数据的授权。
但到2022年ChatGPT成为爆款时，谷歌已经花了很多年时间努力让用户在自己的页面上停留更久。这个最初作为通往更广阔网络的跳板，随着时间推移变成了一个可以直接在搜索结果页上找到答案的地方。发布者再也无法享有像“ 超级碗几点开始 ”这样利润丰厚的套利机会；谷歌会自己回答你的问题。这或许在某种程度上是谷歌的贪婪，但也是对用户需求的明确回应。
我第一次使用ChatGPT时， 在我看来很明显 ，它在各种谷歌搜索上的答案都明显更好。谷歌迟早必须做出回应，而它也确实回应了，推出了AI概览和AI模式。概览是显示在传统搜索顶部的那种方框；AI模式则是一个独立界面，可以从概览进入。无论如何，一年前谷歌高管 曾表示 ，概览的变现效果与传统搜索大致相当；今天这条新闻之所以引起这么多人注意，一个原因就是它暗示AI模式——显然代表着许多高价值品类中搜索的未来——的变现效果并非如此。
需要说明的是，谷歌搜索仍然是一项庞大的业务：其搜索及相关广告收入增长了12%，达到633.5亿美元。但这低于第一季度的19%和第二季度的17%。与上一季度相比，这一数字 基本持平 ，尽管AI模式现在约有 10亿月活用户 ，AI概览约有25亿。（辛德勒没有说明AI模式的收入低多少，也没有说明他具体是在跟什么比较。）

items.title: OpenAI 汇编各方法庭之友意见，主张 AI 训练应适用合理使用原则
items.description: OpenAI 整理了在《纽约时报》诉讼中提交给法院的多份支持合理使用的法庭之友意见摘要，作者包括图书馆协会、法律学者、独立创作者和美国政府等。各意见书主张 AI 训练具有转换性、不构成版权法认可的市场损害，并警告限缩合理使用将阻碍科研进展与美国经济繁荣；完整文件可在法院公开卷宗查阅。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/oas684tt9kpeds9cq7vgjvo1x
items.excerpt:
OpenAI 整理了在《纽约时报》诉讼中提交给法院的多份支持合理使用的法庭之友意见摘要，作者包括图书馆协会、法律学者、独立创作者和美国政府等。各意见书主张 AI 训练具有转换性、不构成版权法认可的市场损害，并警告限缩合理使用将阻碍科研进展与美国经济繁荣；完整文件可在法院公开卷宗查阅。
OpenAI 汇编多领域法庭之友意见，读者可据此了解 AI 训练合理使用抗辩的核心论点与《纽约时报》诉讼的争议焦点。
作者、记者、创作者、学者、无障碍倡导者、法律专家、图书馆员、经济学家和企业领袖纷纷发声，支持合理使用这一由来已久的原则，以及该原则在 AI 训练中的适用。
几十年来，合理使用在推动惠及所有人的创新方面发挥了关键作用。它促成了重要的医学和科学突破，也催生了新技术，为无数人——包括作者和记者——带来了实实在在的积极改变。与此同时， 《纽约时报》的诉讼 却要求所有人无视半个世纪的法律历史与进步，为了自己狭隘的一己之利——一笔本不该得的赔偿——抛弃合理使用这一由来已久的原则。
来自广泛领域的专家和领袖已经认识到，合理使用是一种双赢，惠及所有人；他们向法院提交了支持合理使用的意见书，阐述了自己的观点。
下面摘录了其中部分意见书的内容，均按原文呈现。完整的提交文件可在公开的法院案卷中查阅，你也可以 在这里 进一步了解合理使用与 AI。
美国盲人理事会、研究图书馆协会、美国图书馆协会、消费者技术协会 & 商业软件联盟⁠
法院应当驳回原告试图将版权延伸至既定边界之外的请求。AI 训练对受版权保护作品的使用目的截然不同，不会向公众提供这些作品的替代性获取途径，也不会造成《版权法》所认定的市场损害。相反，它催生了一系列广泛的变革性技术，这些技术已经在带来公共利益。版权的存在是为了促进创造力和进步，而不是压制合法创新，也不是保护作者免受竞争。因此，既定的合理使用原则必然得出这样的结论：生成式 AI 训练属于合理使用。
本案涉及的远不止开发大语言模型（LLM）的公司。它关系到医学研究人员和患者，关系到为有不同学习需求的学生提供服务的教育工作者，关系到寻求更大独立性的残障人士，关系到运用农业知识的农民，关系到探索新表达形式的独立创作者，也关系到从软件到法律等各个行业。这些群体有一个共同利益：能够研究和学习广泛而多样的知识来源，并能获得让这种学习发挥作用的工具。许多人依赖他人开发的系统（包括开源 AI 系统），而不是自己训练模型。合理使用支撑着他们学习、发现、交流和创造的能力。限制对合理使用作品的训练，既会影响构建 AI 的机构，也会影响使用 AI 的人。
市场稀释理论要求版权法保护权利人免受一种它此前从未限制过的经济现象的影响。新作品可能降低旧作品的销量、曝光度或价值，却并未复制其受保护的表达。《版权法》有意将这种竞争置于版权人的控制之外。因此，法庭之友恳请法院裁定：“市场稀释”，即来自非侵权输出的总体竞争压力——包括那些占据相同主题或体裁、具有相同不受保护特征或争夺相同受众的输出——不属于《美国法典》第17编第107条第4款意义上的可认知市场损害。驳回该理论将维护第二巡回法院一贯坚持的区分：版权保护作者免受对其受保护表达的替代，而非免受仅仅与之竞争的新表达的成功。
初创公司对基础模型的使用表明，使用受版权保护的作品训练AI模型属于合理使用，而非版权侵权。训练基础模型的目的是构建一个通用工具，供他人适配新用途，而非复制其学习到的作品。初创公司所选择的用途与任何训练数据集中作品的用途毫无相似之处。
在AI训练能够创造新知识、表达、软件及其他能力的范围内，这些益处会影响第四要素对使用市场影响的评估。这一推理支持在此处的一种新颖应用：考虑那些能够实现新分析、软件及其他生产性工作的能力所具有的国家安全价值。
版权不仅支持创作内容的激励，也支持构建从这些内容中学习的工具的激励；而一项将每一次被替代的销售都视为可诉的规则，可能削弱后者，却无法可靠地保护前者。
AI 是一项变革性技术，能加速艺术与科学无数学科中新作品的创作。Kelly 先生对 AI 如何推动文学领域发展有切身体会。在他看来，每个 AI 模型都可以理解为一个全新的媒介，让作者有能力创作新的文本和思想，并进行推理。因此，若在合理使用问题上判原告胜诉，给予原告的将远远超出国会意图赋予其原创表达的有限垄断权。这会阻碍能够传播前所未有海量信息的技术的发展，也会妨碍新的思维模式以及艺术与科学领域新原创作品的创作。法庭之友提交本意见书，支持被告的论点，即为训练大语言模型而使用受版权保护的作品属于 17 U.S.C. § 107 下的合理使用。基于他毕生从事写作的经历，版权所有者获得的保护对 Kelly 先生很重要。同样至关重要的是，为版权材料的允许使用和变革性技术的发展保留空间。否则，版权将扼杀它本应鼓励的创造力、创新和知识传播。合理使用原则对于确保这种平衡至关重要。
根据本案记录，被告使用原告作品进行 AI 训练具有高度转换性，强烈支持认定合理使用，因为在现实条件下，被告模型的输出与训练过程中产生的不可见中间副本在任何相关方面都不相似。
本意见书通过两位独立创作者的亲身经历，让人一窥这句话在实践中的含义——他们既依赖版权保护， 也 依赖 AI 工具来维持生计。 法庭之友 Sarah Rose Siskind 和 Michael Wall 是创作并授权原创作品的艺术家。但他们用 AI 处理创作过程周边的工作，并在一个充斥着资源更雄厚竞争者的市场中发展自己的事业。对 法庭之友 而言，AI 并未取代创造力，也没有让他们走创作捷径。AI 帮助他们创作更多作品，并将作品延伸到新的表达形式。 法庭之友 的经历印证了美国的观点：AI 工具“能够也应该有助于拉平主流出版商与独立出版商之间的竞争环境”。Siskind 在业务的方方面面都用 AI，从日常行政事务到构思创意、招揽新客户。有了 AI，她的非创作工作更快、成本更低，创作工作也更好。用她的话说：“我觉得现在没有 AI，我的生意根本做不下去。”同样，AI 帮

items.title: OpenRouter 实测 Claude Opus vs Sonnet vs Haiku 5.5 该选哪个
items.description: OpenRouter 实测 Claude Opus 5.5、Sonnet 5.5 与 Haiku 5.5 三档模型，建议默认用 Sonnet 5.5，高频与子智能体任务用 Haiku 5.5，长且容错成本高的任务用 Opus 5.5。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/gzcwy89nkjreenv5eu1qaysdi
items.excerpt:
Claude Opus vs Sonnet vs Haiku: Which Should You Use?
OpenRouter 实测 Claude Opus 5.5、Sonnet 5.5 与 Haiku 5.5 三档模型，建议默认用 Sonnet 5.5，高频与子智能体任务用 Haiku 5.5，长且容错成本高的任务用 Opus 5.5。
把 Claude Sonnet 5.5 设为默认模型，高并发和子智能体任务用 Claude Haiku 5.5 ，任务耗时长、需求模糊或出错代价高时用 Claude Opus 5.5 。
对多数团队来说，选择其实是在 Opus 和 Sonnet 之间做，问题在于 Opus 每 token 的价格是 Sonnet 的两倍，值不值。在我们测试的编程任务上，答案是不值。我们给每个模型都安排了同样的 11 个带隐藏测试的编程任务，以及 Claude Code 里同一个修 bug 任务。所有模型全部通过，所以拉开差距的是成本。按任务算，Haiku 比 Opus 便宜 19 到 30 倍，Sonnet 的成本则是 Opus 的一半到三分之二。
这些结果只说明三款模型在我们任务上的表现。要知道哪款最适合你的工作流，唯一的办法是在你自己的工作上测试。 Ori Eval 可以帮你做这件事。你问编程智能体哪个模型最适合你的项目，它就会在你的代码里找测试素材、编写评测、运行你想对比的模型，并给出推荐，同时附上分数、耗时和成本。后面讲模型切换的那一节会说明如何让它指向这三个层级。
Opus 5.5、Sonnet 5.5 和 Haiku 5.5 是同一代模型的三个层级。Anthropic 于 2026 年 9 月 22 日发布 Opus 5.5 ，9 月 28 日发布 Sonnet 5.5 ，10 月 7 日发布 Haiku 5.5 。三者都有 100 万 token 上下文窗口 ，都接受文本、图片和 PDF。它们的主要差异在价格，另外 Haiku 的基准测试分数更低。
价格是 2026 年 10 月 21 日我们的标价，来自 Opus 5.5 、 Sonnet 5.5 和 Haiku 5.5 的模型页面。基准测试各行来自我们的 benchmarks 接口 ，数据于 10 月 21 日拉取（我们的测试运行于 10 月 17 日）。 Artificial Analysis 智能指数 是独立基准测试公司 Artificial Analysis 对 10 项评测给出的综合分数。T 表示万亿 token，数据来自我们的 每日排名数据集 。
在我们跑的基准测试里，Claude Opus 5.5 并没有胜过 Claude Sonnet 5.5。在我们跑的 GPQA Diamond 上 Sonnet 得分更高，这是一组 198 道研究生水平的科学题（92.4% 对 90.4%）。在 τ-bench airline 上它同样更高，这是一个多轮客服智能体基准（78.7% 对 75.5%）。在 Artificial Analysis 指数上 Opus 领先 1.6 分。在我们两次运行中，Sonnet 每个任务的成本都不到一半：GPQA 每题 $0.025，Opus 是 $0.054；τ-bench 每任务 $0.16，Opus 是 $0.34。
10 月 12 日那一周，Opus 5.5 在 OpenRouter 上的 token 用量约为 Sonnet 的 2.5 倍。Opus 还是 Claude Code 在多数套餐下的 默认模型 ，在我们的测试中，没有指定模型时 Claude Code 会通过 OpenRouter 使用 Opus 5.5。如果你没改过模型，那你跑的就是 Opus。
对于需求明确、常规性的工作，Haiku 5.5 可以取代 Sonnet。它在 τ-bench airline 上得分 76.0%，比 Opus 高半分，比 Sonnet 低 2.7 分，每任务成本 $0.011，约为 Sonnet 的十四分之一。我们每个模型跑了 100 到 200 个任务，所以这个基准上几分之差可能是噪声。在 GPQA Diamond 上 Haiku 落后 Sonnet 5.8 分，在 Artificial Analysis 指数上落后 12.6 分——该指数中智能体任务和通用知识各占 30%，编程和科学推理各占 20%。在常规编程上，我们下面的测试没有发现差距。
我们测了两件事：按规格写函数，以及用 Claude Code 修一个代码仓库。三个模型在两项测试中都通过了全部测试。
我们写了 11 个 Python 任务，每个都配一个隐藏测试文件。8 个日常任务是：解析时长、合并区间、LRU 缓存、不用 eval 的算术求值器、cron 表达式的下次运行时间、自动换行、 语义化版本 排序，以及 JSON 路径读取器。3 个困难任务分别是：不用 re 模块的正则引擎、带三值 NULL 逻辑的 SQL WHERE 过滤器，以及夏令时切换日跨时区的空闲日程时段。每个模型对每个日常任务作答两次、每个困难任务作答三次，使用模型默认设置，每个模型共 25 次尝试。
Haiku 用的推理最多，却仍然最快完成困难任务。在困难任务上它平均用了 3,202 个 推理 token ，Opus 是 1,252 个。推理 token 是模型在写出答案之前用于推演问题的 token。即便推理更多，Haiku 每个困难任务的成本也只有 Opus 的二十七分之一。

items.description: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy 在周四的季度财报电话会议上表示，AWS 未来五到十年内可以成为年营收万亿美元的业务，2026 年现金 capex 预计约 2200 亿美元，大部分投向 AWS，2027 年还将大幅增加。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/fxmexzrmo7pw52vc5j6ej17kl
items.excerpt:
AWS will be a $1T business, Jassy says — but first, it will spend big
Amazon CEO Andy Jassy 在周四的季度财报电话会议上表示，AWS 未来五到十年内可以成为年营收万亿美元的业务，2026 年现金 capex 预计约 2200 亿美元，大部分投向 AWS，2027 年还将大幅增加。
原文给出 AWS 最新财报数字、2026 约 2200 亿美元 capex 计划和 Jassy 的万亿营收时间表，可帮助读者判断云厂商 AI 投入节奏。
Andy Jassy 已经 公开表示 ，他相信 AWS 能成为一项年收入达万亿美元的业务。在周四亚马逊的季度财报电话会议上，他重申了这一雄心。
“我们在亚马逊打造的东西是前所未有的。历史上从来没有一家企业做到过一万亿美元的年度营收，”他说。
不过，在云业务达到那一步之前，亚马逊需要加大资本支出，建设支撑这项蓬勃业务所需的基础设施。
“我们仍预计 2026 年的现金资本支出约为 2200 亿美元——其中大部分用于 AWS——并预计 2027 年的支出会明显更多，而且我们清楚地看到这些投入能带来财务回报，”Jassy 周四透露。
亚马逊在 AI 基础设施上的巨额投入，今年一直是 投资者担忧的来源 。在周四的电话会议上，华尔街分析师确实反复要求 Jassy 解释这些支出、增长真的会到来的信号，以及预期的利润率。
Jassy 告诉他们，这些钱都花得值，因为这家电商巨头计划抓住由 AI 驱动的全球云需求的历史性时刻。AWS 收入同比增长 39%，这已是 连续第六个季度 保持稳步增长。
“AWS 是一项年化收入运行率达到 1840 亿美元的业务，但机会依然非同寻常，”这位 CEO 兴奋地说。“凭借我们持续的创新步伐、新的核心功能和 AI 功能、企业希望在 AWS 上运行其核心和 AI 工作负载，以及我们每年新增的容量，我们相信 AWS 在 2027 年和 2028 年都能增长 40% 以上，并在未来五到十年内成为一项万亿美元收入的业务。”
Jassy 还补充说，企业采用 AI 仍处于“非常早期的阶段”，并表示到目前为止，“这一战略正在奏效”。
后来，当被问及为何发展 AWS 所需的投资如此巨大时，Jassy 将 AI 热潮形容为“一生一次的机会”，认为现在需要、也值得做出如此巨大的财务承诺。
“我们会继续投资，以保持领先地位，”他说。“我们有能力为这一计划提供资金，我认为它将永远改变亚马逊的规模。它将永远改变我们的收入。”
AI 热潮对云行业来说喜忧参半，因为支撑这股热潮的 AI 服务依赖云基础设施。和亚马逊一样，其他云服务商也在 大举支出 ，但同时也在大把赚钱。例如，微软 刚刚公布 了又一份创纪录的收入增长，主要由其云业务驱动。它同样 花了一大笔钱 。
当您通过我们文章中的链接购买时， 我们可能会赚取少量佣金 。这不会影响我们的编辑独立性。
Lucas 是 TechCrunch 的高级撰稿人，负责报道人工智能、消费科技和初创企业。他此前在 Gizmodo 报道 AI 和网络安全。 您可以通过发送邮件至 [email protected] 联系 Lucas。

items.description: Alphabet 因 AI 搜索概要影响广告收入，单日市值从 3.97 万亿跌至 3.46 万亿美元，缩水超 5000 亿美元。该季度总营收增 25% 至 1276 亿美元，云业务营收增 103% 至近 310 亿美元，但利润下降 25%，自由现金流为负超 90 亿美元。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/puushryi79v0flh2um3a70xnw
items.excerpt:
Google value plunges by $500B as AI fears rattle Wall Street
Alphabet 因 AI 搜索概要影响广告收入，单日市值从 3.97 万亿跌至 3.46 万亿美元，缩水超 5000 亿美元。该季度总营收增 25% 至 1276 亿美元，云业务营收增 103% 至近 310 亿美元，但利润下降 25%，自由现金流为负超 90 亿美元。
原文梳理了 Google、Amazon、Microsoft 三家财报中 AI 投入与现金流变化的具体数字，读者可对比资本市场的不同反应。
谷歌母公司Alphabet周四市值蒸发逾5000亿美元（3740亿英镑），此前其年内最后一次业务运营更新令华尔街大为震动。
谷歌披露其搜索业务中的人工智能（AI）摘要正在影响广告收入，这让投资者如此恐慌，以至于公司股价跌至六个月低点。
微软和亚马逊本周也向投资者做了更新，并与谷歌一道，计划在这场持续进行的人工智能竞赛中继续投入天文数字的资金。
总营收同比增长25%，达到1276亿美元。这得益于谷歌云业务的持续成功，其营收增长103%，接近310亿美元。
然而，公司本季度利润大幅下滑25%。而且，作为上市公司， 历史上第二次 出现负自由现金流，这次超过90亿美元，几乎是Alphabet三个月前现金亏损额的两倍。
现金流代表公司在支付运营和投资费用后留存的资金，这意味着Alphabet如今花的钱比赚的钱还多。这一新增的支出水平几乎全部用于谷歌的人工智能投资。
谷歌无处不在的搜索引擎如今默认对用户的查询给出AI摘要，这影响了本季度它能够售出的广告数量。
Forrester首席分析师特蕾西·吴表示，Alphabet令人失望的搜索业务业绩“凸显了在为大规模AI投资提供资金的同时维持成熟业务实力所面临的挑战”。
尽管谷歌首席商务官菲利普·辛德勒周三表示，他对搜索引擎以AI为核心的版本“非常看好我们的发展轨迹”，但公司股价周四仍下跌近13%，为今年第二低的表现。
除了季度销售额增长11%、达到2010亿美元之外，公司还公布了一个惊人的现金流数字：负420亿美元。
首席执行官安迪·贾西称，公司加大支出部分是因为它有机会拥有不止一项、而是两项未来可能为亚马逊带来1万亿美元收入的业务。
贾西没有具体说明这两项业务是什么。但在与金融分析师的电话会议上，他多次提到亚马逊自研自销电脑芯片带来的财务机会，以及其AI开发者平台Bedrock——该平台让付费用户可以使用大多数主流AI模型和工具。
“20多年来我们学到的一个教训是，没有哪一种工具能统治世界，”贾西说。“人们总是以为早期领先的东西就会是人们唯一使用的东西——从来都不是这样。”
贾西被多次要求解释公司的支出，他承认如果这笔钱分摊到未来25年“会更方便”。“但现实并非如此，”他补充道。
“我们有能力为这个计划提供资金，我认为它将永远改变亚马逊的规模、营收和自由现金流。”
该公司也是OpenAI最大的投资者之一，其在专门用于AI的投资上少花了约50亿美元。本周早些时候它还透露 计划裁减数千名员工 ，这将进一步降低公司成本。
与此同时，其营收同比增长19%，本季度达到923亿美元。其关键的云业务增长30%，达到630亿美元。
首席执行官萨提亚·纳德拉表示，微软的AI聊天机器人和工具Copilot的使用量“自7月以来自动化任务几乎翻了一番”，日活用户同比增长500%。
“微软的业绩印证了企业对AI的需求依然强劲，但也凸显出科技行业面临的一个更大的问题：AI的价值最终将在哪里被捕获，”Woo说。

Tariffs and geopolitical pressures are among the key external factors slowing progress, but internal gaps persist as well, State of Supply Chain Sustainability report shows.
Corporate commitment to sustainability has reached a record high, but oversight is lagging and external disruptions are keeping companies from delivering transformational results. That’s according to the 2026 State of Supply Chain Sustainability report from the MIT Sustainable Supply Chain Lab at the MIT Center for Transportation and Logistics (MIT CTL), released this month.
Researchers surveyed 1,810 supply chain professionals across 91 countries and found that 83% rate sustainability as important or very important to long-term business success, the highest level in the report’s seven-year history. What’s more, the report found that corporate commitment has grown despite recent shifts in U.S. climate policy, with 59% saying they have become more committed to sustainability while just 13% say they have become less committed.
Those advances are being tempered by outside factors. Nearly 70% of respondents said that tariff uncertainty has forced their organizations to delay, scale back, or compromise sustainability strategies, and more than eight in 10 said that geopolitical conflict is reducing the effectiveness of climate action.
Internal problems exist as well: The study also found that companies’ public sustainability ambition is outpacing the governance and accountability needed to deliver results.
“Companies with formal cross-functional sustainability teams are far more likely to embed sustainability in everyday decisions: 57% do so frequently or always, compared with 13% where responsibility sits within a single function,” according to the report. “Yet only 51% of companies with public sustainability goals have a formal cross-functional team, and only 33% place oversight at board level. Many companies have set the direction but have not yet built the internal structures needed to turn those commitments into consistent action.”
The effects of geopolitics and governance is just one of four themes examined in the report. The research also evaluates where sustainability efforts “live” in the supply chain, how artificial intelligence is affecting sustainability goals, and how warehousing and freight transportation operations are progressing toward decarbonization.

Nearly half of Americans who use artificial intelligence to help them shop have later returned the AI-recommended item, a survey from supply chain software firm Blue Yonder has found.
Online shoppers increasingly come in contact with an AI tool or assistant, such as a consumer chatbot. Of the 24% of U.S. consumers who have purchased a product after receiving an AI recommendation from that source, nearly half (46%) have returned one in the past year. The top reasons for U.S. shoppers returning an AI-recommended purchase are that it was different than described (36%) or was an incorrect size or fit (23%).
That order reverses for U.S. returns overall, where incorrect size or fit leads at 42% and different than described accounts for only 20%. The pattern suggests AI tools struggle less with fit than with describing products accurately.
Those numbers came from Dallas-based Blue Yonder’s fourth annual “2026 Consumer Retail Returns Survey,” which polled more than 5,000 consumers across the U.S., Australia, France, Germany and the U.K., including 2,000 Americans.
“Shoppers are taking AI’s advice faster than retailers are getting ready for it, and nearly half of them are sending something back,” said Duncan Angove, CEO of Blue Yonder. “That’s not really an AI problem. It’s a data problem. An AI assistant is only as good as the product information it can find, and most product data was written for a search bar, not for a machine suggesting products for someone. When what arrives doesn’t match what the shopper expected, it goes back in the box.”

Anthropic’s financials are surprisingly strong
作者通读 Anthropic 公开版 S-1 文件，认为公司财务状况好于预期：2026 年第二季度收入从一季度的 47 亿美元增至 116 亿美元，并录得首个运营利润，截至 6 月底现金储备仅次于 Google 和 Berkshire Hathaway。
作者通读 Anthropic 公开的 S-1 文件，用现金流和季度收入数据说明其财务状况与算力承诺之间的张力。
今年6月，Anthropic向美国证券交易委员会 秘密提交了S-1表格的草稿 ，这是其向公众发行股票的关键一步。周一，Anthropic 宣布 已提交同一文件的公开版本。我通读了全文，从中了解到不少关于公司财务状况的信息——至少截至今年6月30日的情况是如此。
总体来看，公司的财务状况出奇地好。2025年至2026年初，营收大幅飙升，使公司在第二季度首次实现营业利润。截至6月底，Anthropic的现金储备超过了除谷歌和伯克希尔·哈撒韦之外的所有非银行企业。
不过，未来几年对这家AI巨头来说可能充满挑战。出于对持续增长的预期，Anthropic已承诺向亚马逊、谷歌、SpaceXAI、博通等公司投入数千亿美元用于算力。要收回这些支出，Anthropic的年营收需要增长到数千亿美元。
Anthropic尚未正式公布第三季度营收，但 媒体 报道 显示其营收增速有所放缓。营收从2026年第一季度的47亿美元跃升至第二季度的116亿美元，第三季度为168亿美元。按常规企业标准衡量，这仍是惊人的增长，但增速已低于上一季度。
因此，Anthropic财务状况最大的悬念在于：第三季度营收为何没有增长得更快——以及这对未来意味着什么。或许Anthropic的营收将在未来一年继续指数级增长，那样的话，公司轻松就能支付其算力承诺。
但也可能Claude Code和Anthropic其他产品的需求正接近饱和。若果真如此，第四季度及以后的营收增速可能进一步放缓，届时公司可能难以兑现已经做出的数千亿美元支出承诺。

items.title: The Exception Backlog: Supply Chain’s Overlooked Operational Constraint
items.description: The Exception Backlog: Supply Chain's Overlooked Operational Constraint identifies a queue that many logistics organizations feel every day but rarely measure: unresolved exceptions waiting for human attention. The post The Exception Backlog: Supply Chain’s Overlooked Operational Constraint appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Unresolved exceptions form a queue that many logistics organizations feel every day but rarely measure. When exceptions arrive faster than planners can investigate, coordinate, and close them, the backlog becomes an operating constraint just like dock congestion, labor shortage, or insufficient carrier capacity.
Each exception has an arrival time, service time, priority, and outcome. Some take seconds; others require multiple systems, partners, approvals, and calls. When arrival rate exceeds resolution capacity, work accumulates. Aging increases and more cases miss the window in which an inexpensive intervention was still possible. The backlog is another form of the decision bottleneck : unresolved work consumes operating capacity even when the physical network still has trucks, doors, labor, and inventory available.
Planner attention is finite. Time spent assembling context, chasing status, copying information, and routing approvals is capacity that cannot be used for optimization, relationship management, or novel problems. The organization can have sufficient physical assets and still underperform because decision work is queued.
AEM is moving toward selective autonomy: routine, high-frequency, bounded exceptions are increasingly handled by software while people focus on ambiguity, relationships, policy conflicts, and high-consequence decisions The highest leverage often comes from automating context assembly and repetitive resolution steps before automating the final decision. Even when a human retains approval, reducing research and administrative work can materially increase throughput.
Track open exceptions by class, age, business consequence, and owner. Measure median and tail resolution times, percentage resolved before the intervention deadline, recurrence, and auto-resolution rate. These measures make the constraint visible and help distinguish a technology problem from a policy, data, or staffing problem.
Not every exception deserves the same service level. High-value, time-sensitive issues should move through a fast lane. Low-consequence deviations may be suppressed or handled automatically. The operating model should allocate human judgment where its marginal value is highest.
Once the backlog is treated as a real queue, exception management becomes measurable. The objective is not to eliminate every exception; it is to build enough decision-and-action capacity that important exceptions are resolved before they become expensive.

How I Built the Most AI-Pilled Company in the World . Don't be put off by the clickbait headline, this piece by Jacob Sansbury describing how they are building Spawn is a fascinating exploration of the bleeding edge of what's possible with agentic engineering against frontier models.
Spawn is a massively multiplayer gaming environment where players can use prompts (to the in-game agent, Savi) to modify the game world.
I fired it up on my phone for a few minutes and was able to prompt a castle into existence, then a dragon, then ride the dragon to fly around that castle.
By Jacob's telling, Spawn is now being developed autonomously by a swarm of Fable-powered agents costing over $3 million in tokens per month ("we spend 30x payroll on AI tokens").
Our agents change the live code directly and ship to production hourly, so they read every error, bug report and metric themselves. About 60% of our work starts from a production error, a Savi bug report (Savi is the AI you build games with in Spawn), something odd in our logs, or a feature request.
Savi files bugs herself. When a user hits one, or Savi hits one in the product, she files it. It goes straight to an agent that decides whether it's a real bug to fix, something we won't fix, or intentional design that needs a decision. Usually it becomes a change, delivered to that user within an hour, with a message in the same chat.
This is continuous deployment turned up to 11:
A loop this tight only works if it never stops, so we treat an hour without a ship as a SEV-0, our most severe kind of incident. Unshipped changes pile up, and every problem already in production lasts longer. The feedback slows down too. An agent can only keep a few hours of work in its head, so shipping faster than that actually helps it stay coherent. [...]
We can roll back a broken change in 30 seconds, exactly where it's broken and nowhere else. When a monitor or a log alert fires, it starts or wakes an agent that owns the incident, and we break things on purpose to test that those recovery paths work.

OpenAI 更新其公开的 Model Spec，将指导原则重组为五项核心价值观：忠实于人类意图、最小化伤害、诚实透明、促进人类自主和关怀。更新新增了关于上下文理解、监督和自主性的指导，调整了部分行为默认值，退出了大部分详细风格指南，并将模型称呼从 the assistant 改为 GPT。
随着我们的模型越来越智能，在现实世界中采取的行动也越来越有分量，它们不能只停留在理解收到的具体指令上，这一点正变得愈发重要。模型还需要理解人类的意图和价值观，这样才能在指令没有明确覆盖的情况下做出良好判断，同时始终忠于人类意图并接受人类监督。
今天我们更新了 模型规范（在新窗口打开） ，这是我们公开说明希望模型如何行为的文件。此次更新围绕五项基本价值重新组织了规范内容： 忠于人类意图 、 尽量减少伤害 、 诚实与透明 、 尊重人的自主性 以及 关怀 。这体现了我们在 价值对齐 方面的工作目标：让模型在陌生情境中理解并运用人类价值观，同时始终忠于人类意图。除了对现有原则作出更清晰的解释，本次修订还新增了关于情境、监督和自主性的指引，调整了一些默认行为，并删去了大部分详细的风格指引。
上述五项价值阐明了模型规范中早已体现的广泛承诺：服务于人类目的、保持真实、尽量减少伤害、尊重人们形成自身观点的自由，以及认真对待人们的处境。把这些承诺汇聚在一起，有助于解释规范为何要求模型以特定方式行事，也帮助我们在这些承诺表达得不够充分的地方制定更清晰的指引。此次更新是我们 完善规范工作 的又一步，依托于研究、部署模型的经验、 公众对规范及模型行为的反馈 ，以及与用户和外部专家的讨论。
忠于人类意图 是这一方法的根基：理解并帮助人们追求对他们重要的事情。OpenAI 负责撰写规范、设定边界，并训练模型遵守这些边界；开发者在这一边界内指导应用；用户则在上述约束下指导模型的工作。我们的模型应当 拓展人们塑造自身生活的能力 ，帮助他们理解世界、发现可能性、追求自己选定的目标，同时认真对待这种协助对他人造成的影响。忠于人类意图与其余四项价值共同构成了规范的组织框架，指导模型如何权衡它们面临的一些最重要取舍。这些价值并不意在涵盖模型应当尊重并帮助人们追求的全部人类价值。
忠实意味着不止于字面执行指令，而是深入理解 OpenAI、开发者和用户的意图与价值取向，并在这种理解不完整时做出明智判断。它还意味着要认识到人们的信念和价值观会变化，帮助他们以自己认可的方式反思和成长，而不是悄悄引导他们或替他们做选择。例如，在帮人比较工作机会时，模型可以援引对方此前分享过的优先考虑——比如希望工作时间可预测——同时把这些假设摆到明面上，方便对方纠正。
我们的使命是确保通用人工智能造福全人类。这要求我们不仅考虑某人当下的意图，还要考虑其长远利益以及对他人造成的影响。另外四项价值观把这些考量明确表达出来：
诚实与透明 ，意味着如实说明模型知道什么、做了什么、对什么不确定，让人们能够理解和评估它的推理与工作。
关怀 ，意味着关注受影响者的处境，遵循相关的社会与职业规范，并让人们可以信赖模型的工作。
《模型规范》把这些价值观转化为可操作的指引：在需要保护人和社会的地方设定明确边界，其余部分大多以默认规则的形式呈现，用户和开发者可以覆盖。
在更新《模型规范》的同时，我们一直在探索新的训练方法，帮助模型学习这些核心价值观，更好地理解和遵循规范中的具体行为原则。目标是让模型理解这些原则为何重要，以及如何在新情境中运用它们： 做正确的事 ， 出于正确的理由 。我们希望这种理解能支撑模型在重大决策上做出合理判断，在日常决策中保持审慎——这些日常决策累积起来，可以 为人和社会带来持久益处（在新窗口打开） 。我们会在后续更新中分享这项训练工作的成果和经验。
这次重组还帮助我们找出了哪些地方需要补充指引，据此制定新原则，并按需修订或停用原有指引。
新增的“忠实于人类意图”一节，出发点是：人们所看重的东西是第一位的，而指令通常是这些价值最清晰、最重要的信号。这一思路借鉴了对齐研究中的“协助博弈”框架（参见 早期工作（在新窗口打开） 和 后续综述（在新窗口打开） ）。该节纳入了更新后的 指令链（在新窗口打开） ，说明哪些指令适用、冲突如何解决。新增小节 仔细考虑上下文（在新窗口打开） 则说明对话、记忆和其他上下文证据应如何帮助模型理解人们的意图和偏好。
我们还为 支持人的能动性⁠（在新窗口打开） 和 遵循相关社会规范⁠（在新窗口打开） 补充了默认要求，并扩充了关于 控制并沟通副作用⁠（在新窗口打开） 的现有指引。这些原则涵盖了其余价值观在模型行为中体现的更多方式——它们往往细微却重要：考虑工作成果对他人的影响、增强用户的能力、产出人们可以信赖的成果，同时尊重用户的目标和指令。
与此同时，我们删去了规范中大部分详细的风格指引。风格应当顺应人们的偏好——既包括语言和文化层面的整体偏好，也包括每个人的个人偏好——而用户反馈和具体情境则为这些偏好提供依据。规范保留了更强的默认要求，例如 客观地探讨问题⁠（在新窗口打开） 。用户和开发者可以明确要求模型采取特定视角，但模型不应仅仅因为觉得对方想听什么，就推断出这种偏好。
最后，考虑到模型用例和部署场景日益广泛，我们在规范中现在称模型为“GPT”，而不再称“助手”。
随着模型能力不断增强，本次更新是让规范背后的价值观和推理更加明确的第一步。模型规范描述的是我们努力实现的行为，我们的模型尚未完全体现这一点。我们将从研究、实际使用和反馈中不断学习，持续改进规范与模型。
我们想知道你认为规范中哪些部分有说服力、哪些地方你不认同其权衡取舍，以及它忽略了什么或哪些地方表述不清。关于价值观、权衡取舍和具体措辞的反馈，能帮助我们改进规范。欢迎阅读 更新后的模型规范⁠（在新窗口打开） 并 分享你的看法⁠（在新窗口打开） 。

items.title: Can Frontier Models See Past a Decoy? Elorian Tests Visual Reasoning
items.description: A new decoy counting benchmark exposes a gap between seeing and reasoning. Elorian’s Glimpse tries to bridge it by thinking with images.
items.excerpt:
A new decoy counting benchmark exposes a gap between seeing and reasoning. Elorian’s Glimpse tries to bridge it by thinking with images.
This month Elorian launched its first visual reasoning model , Glimpse . It’s being promoted as “a new category of visual thinking model: a system that reasons about the physical world from what it sees.”
So how does Glimpse compare to both frontier models and world models in vision tests? A new benchmark called DecoyCount , co-released by Elorian, provides some answers.
We quizzed CEO Andrew Dai on the benchmark, and also talked about Elorian’s positioning in a crowded models landscape.
Elorian emerged from stealth in April with $55 million in seed funding , co-led by Striker Venture Partners, Menlo Ventures and Altimeter Capital. Now, in partnership with AI data company Mercor , Elorian is announcing the DecoyCount benchmark, which tests whether language models genuinely count objects or rely on visual shortcuts and substitution heuristics.
According to a paper accompanying the release , frontier models scored below 50% accuracy on DecoyCount — the highest was GPT-6 Astra, with 43.17%. Elorian’s new model isn’t mentioned in the paper, but Dai told us that Glimpse scored 50.48% in an internal test.
Regarding the frontier models, the paper concludes that “stronger general reasoning does not by itself generalize to aligned visual reasoning.”
How the benchmark works: “DecoyCount exposes interpretable counting failures across seven mechanisms.”
To make sure it was a like-for-like comparison with the frontier models, we asked whether the paper’s evaluation images were withheld from Glimpse’s training?
“The evaluation images and text were withheld from our training, and our contamination check found no overlap in the training data checked,” Dai replied, via email. “Without any cues, Glimpse scored 50.48% on the 1,660 DecoyCount items, making it the only model in the comparison to clear 50%. The closest was GPT-6 Astra at 43.17%, about 7 points behind, and Gemini-3.8-flash scored 32.71% while Qwen3.8-max scored 28.31%, and Claude-Fable-5.1 came in at 25.22%.”
Dai did note that Glimpse’s results “come from a single run of the model on its own, without an agent or tool harness,” whereas the six models from the paper were each averaged across three runs under their reported settings.

items.title: OpenAI 详解如何监控前沿模型的失对齐行为
items.description: OpenAI 在 Alignment 博客介绍其针对前沿模型（如 GPT-6 Astra）的多层失对齐监控系统，覆盖训练、评估、内部使用和部分外部部署。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/e234ewhx82g2zh3z2bgcjxx7d
items.excerpt:
How we detect frontier model misalignment
OpenAI 在 Alignment 博客介绍其针对前沿模型（如 GPT-6 Astra）的多层失对齐监控系统，覆盖训练、评估、内部使用和部分外部部署。
OpenAI 公开了内部失对齐监控系统的分层架构、检出率数据和红队结果，读者可以据此了解前沿模型监控的实际做法与局限。
随着我们训练能力越来越强的 AI 模型，我们需要可靠的手段来发现模型行为何时偏离了我们的预期。智能体可能在训练、评估或部署过程中出现不当行为、采取未经授权的操作，后果可能很严重。为了发现这些故障，并在必要时及时干预，我们会监控智能体的推理过程、它采取的行动，以及这些行动对其环境造成的影响。
我们 监控内部编程智能体 已有一段时间，但 Hugging Face 事件 暴露出我们覆盖范围中的一个缺口：该事件始于内部网络安全评估，而我们当时并未在这些评估中运行失准行为监控。针对这起事件，也考虑到我们模型 整体能力的提升 ，我们大幅扩展了智能体行为监控系统。如今，我们的失准监控覆盖前沿模型在更多场景下的行为，包括训练、评估、内部使用，以及外部部署（具体会视产品场景做相应调整）。
为了检验这套扩展后的系统本可以如何帮助阻止 Hugging Face 事件，我们用强化后的监控重放了该事件中记录的行为。在模拟中，智能体首次逃出沙箱约 30 分钟后，监控系统就向安全团队发出了警报，比实际事件中 Hugging Face 系统被攻破的时间早了 30 多个小时。我们认为，这一预警本可以让响应人员有充足时间，在我们的模型能够访问外部服务之前就中断相关活动。
9 月，我们看到了响应人员如何利用一次实时训练运行中的警报。一个模型找到了从本应隔离的环境中 接入互联网 的方法。监控在 15 分钟内标记了这次突破，响应人员三分钟后就着手审查。随后我们暂停了前沿强化学习，同时加固用于约束智能体的系统。
这套监控系统需要消耗大量算力，但我们认为，随着模型能力增强、模型失准的潜在后果加重，这笔成本值得付出。监控是我们 纵深防御 策略中抵御模型失准行为危害的若干层之一。对齐训练旨在降低模型做出有害行为的倾向；安全控制 限制智能体能够访问或影响的系统 ；而当这些防护措施失效时，监控帮助我们发现有遗漏的故障，在危害发生前介入，并从问题中吸取教训。我们认为， 所有模型开发者 都应监控其最强模型的行为。
对于能力至少与 GPT-6 Astra 相当的模型，我们会监控每一次强化学习（RL）运行和评估，以及任何支持工具使用的运行框架。对于大多数工作负载（包括 RL 和评估），我们还会监控那些我们评估为能力超过 GPT-5.5 Thinking 的模型。此外，无论使用哪个模型，我们都会监控所有内部 Codex 流量。这套系统的一个版本还会监控能力超过我们 预备框架 中网络安全能力关键阈值的模型的外部工具使用情况，详见本文下文。
为了在高效利用算力的同时检测事件，我们把监控系统设计成多层架构。第一层筛查阶段投入的算力相对较少，目标是在这一层尽可能多地捕获可疑案例：这些阶段的设计原则是宁可放行、也不漏掉，即使证据尚不明确也先往下传。后续阶段则可以在每个案例上投入更多算力，弄清发生了什么、模型行为是否值得担忧，以及我们是否需要介入。
我们的第一层（L0）使用一类轻量级分类器，称为 激活探针 。它们会在模型的内部激活中寻找可疑模式，并把标记出的案例交给下一层审查。我们把这些探针调向高召回率，宁可接受一些误报，也要降低漏掉可疑行为的概率。
由于我们仍在评估这些探针检测陌生失准形式的效果，我们还会把探针未标记的流量随机抽取 5% 送给下一层。审查这部分样本有助于我们发现探针可能漏掉的可疑行为。考虑到探针的敏感度，我们让前沿 RL 运行和内部 Codex 流量跳过这一层，直接进入下一层。
在下一层（L1），一个基于模型的审查器会检查智能体近期的对话、思维链和工具使用情况，寻找欺骗、未经授权的操作以及试图操纵评估的迹象。审查器使用的是智能体行动时所处的同一个上下文窗口。如果智能体早先的工作已被摘要压缩进受审查的上下文窗口，审查器看到的就是那份摘要。
对于前沿 RL 运行和内部 Codex 流量，我们在每一轮结束时执行一次 L1 检查，并在智能体为腾出上下文窗口空间而摘要其早先工作时也执行一次。我们目前正转向一种新安排：两次检查之间的间隔不超过 30 分钟。
一旦知道智能体被要求做什么，它的行为看起来可能就大不一样了。当 L1 审查器标记出某个案例时，该案例会被送到下一层（L2），由我们的调查智能体进一步检查。这个调查智能体可以核查评估的目的，并且在完整记录可用时，回读智能体所有上下文窗口，弄清它是如何做出这些行动的。调查智能体还能在隔离环境中编写并运行代码来检查相关证据，然后利用发现的结果还原事件经过、识别重复报告，并判断该案例的严重程度。
我们针对不同目的使用不同的调查智能体。安全调查员负责寻找可能需要人工介入的迹象，比如智能体逃出沙箱，或未经授权访问系统。对齐调查员则负责寻找值得研究的行为，即便这些行为没有直接的安全风险。在两类调查员同时启用的场景下，每个被 L1 层标记的案例都会由两者分别审查。我们目前正在把对齐调查推广到更多内部工作负载中。
对于敏感工作负载，包括内部的 Codex 使用、评估和强化学习（RL）运行，下一层（L3）会做进一步检查，依据的是对话之外的证据。安全调查员会把对话记录与网络日志、其他系统遥测数据以及以往案例的证据进行比对，判断是否需要通知人工响应人员。在 L3，对齐审查员还会跨案例比对报告，找出严重故障和反复出现的模式，并对前沿 RL 运行做更深入的检查。
